O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Em vitória de Lula: Senado aprova PEC da Segurança Pública em dois turnos
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
No início da noite desta terça-feira (3), o Senado aprovou a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) 18, de 2025, chamada de PEC da Segurança Pública, em dois turnos. O texto foi aprovado com 73 votos favoráveis e nenhum contrário, no primeiro turno, e por 75 votos a favor e nenhum contra, no segundo. O texto segue para promulgação do Congresso Nacional.
A PEC foi aprovada sem emendas e a aprovação é considerada uma vitória de articulação do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). O ex-ouvidor das Polícias de São Paulo Benedito Mariano avalia que a PEC da Segurança Pública permitirá ter uma política nacional que será eficaz no combate às facções criminosas, sobretudo no eixo de asfixia financeira.
“É o andar de cima do crime que alimenta as ações violentas do crime nas periferias, nos morros. Portanto, tem que ter uma ação concomitante de enfrentamento ao crime no andar de cima e, gradativamente, ir retomando os territórios ocupados pelo crime com uma pasta específica da segurança pública”, afirmou.
Durante o dia, o texto foi alvo de debates porque a oposição tentava inserir no texto a redução da maioridade penal. O PL apresentou proposta para que a maioridade penal diminua para 16 anos, em casos de crimes de menor gravidade, e para 14 anos nos casos de crimes hediondos.
Já o PT admite discutir a redução da maioridade penal para 16 anos apenas para crimes hediondos, mantendo para os demais. Essa ideia foi defendida pelo presidente Lula durante a campanha eleitoral.
A alteração, no entanto, faria o texto retornar à Câmara para uma nova votação. O tema, no entanto, não foi aprovado e será objeto de discussão em projetos específicos.
Ação federal
Proposta pelo governo Lula, a PEC da Segurança Pública estabelece novas regras para a organização da segurança pública no país, amplia a cooperação entre União, estados e municípios e fortalece os mecanismos de enfrentamento ao crime organizado.
Entre outras medidas, a PEC propõe a constitucionalização do Sistema Único de Segurança Pública (SUSP), alterando o Artigo 144 da Carta Magna, que trata da segurança pública.
A proposta inclui que a segurança deve ser exercida “em regime de cooperação federativa” e “por meio da atuação integrada e descentralizada” das diferentes instituições que trabalham com o tema.
“Art. 144-A. Os órgãos de segurança pública articular-se-ão em regime de cooperação federativa, por meio do Sistema Único de Segurança Pública, destinado a assegurar a eficiência da prevenção, da persecução e da execução penal”, define o texto.
Com isso, fica estabelecida a base para criação do Ministério da Segurança Pública, proposto por Lula.
Facções e milícias
Além de penas mais duras para chefes de facções e milícias, a PEC restringe ou veda a progressão de regime, do aberto para o semiaberto, por exemplo, para lideranças dessas organizações, que terão que cumprir penas em unidades de segurança máxima.
Também são previstas medidas patrimoniais contra o produto do crime, a responsabilização de pessoas jurídicas envolvidas e a proteção a denunciantes e seus familiares.
Outra novidade da PEC é a possibilidade de criação de polícias municipais de natureza civil, submetidas ao controle externo do Ministério Público, com a atribuição de realizar policiamento ostensivo e comunitário no âmbito das cidades onde atuarão.
A PEC ainda amplia atribuições da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), prevê a criação de polícias municipais e aumenta a vinculação do orçamento público para segurança pública.
A proposta também prevê a criação do Sistema de Políticas Penais, responsável pelo sistema prisional brasileiro, e autoriza União, estados e municípios a atuarem conjuntamente na legislação sobre segurança pública, organização de polícias, guardas municipais e sistema socioeducativo.
Fundos de financiamento
Segundo a PEC, 50% dos recursos do Fundo Nacional de Segurança Pública (FNSP) e do Fundo Penitenciário Nacional (Funpen) serão repassados pela União para os estados e municípios, excluídas despesas de custeio e investimento da polícia penitenciária nacional do Funpen.
“As regras de financiamento fortalecem o FNSP e o Funpen, criam vinculações e blindagens orçamentárias e garantem repasses obrigatórios. Essas medidas aumentam a previsibilidade financeira, garantindo a perenidade das ações policiais”, escreveu o relator da PEC na CCJ, senador Rogério Carvalho (PT-SE).
A PEC ainda prevê que 10% do superávit financeiro anual do Fundo Social, ligado ao pré-sal, sejam destinados aos fundos da segurança, “reforçando o financiamento contínuo das políticas nacionais de segurança pública e execução penal”.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Cruzeiro critica proibição das bets no STF; governo federal aponta danos à saúde pública
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A proibição das plataformas de apostas esportivas, as chamadas bets, pode provocar desequilíbrio financeiro entre os clubes brasileiros e seus concorrentes sul-americanos. O argumento foi apresentado pelo advogado José Francisco Manssur, representante do Cruzeiro, durante audiência pública realizada nesta terça-feira (3), no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), para discutir a Medida Provisória (MP) nº 1.394/2026, que determinou o fim das apostas de quota fixa e dos cassinos online no Brasil.
Ao defender os interesses do clube mineiro, Manssur argumentou que a medida compromete receitas previstas em contratos de patrocínio firmados antes da proibição. Segundo ele, a manutenção das parcerias comerciais com empresas de apostas por equipes de outros países pode colocar o futebol brasileiro em desvantagem.
“Especialmente entre os nossos clubes e os clubes dos nossos rivais argentinos, que continuarão tendo as bets em suas camisas”, afirmou.
O Atlético Mineiro, por sua vez, não enviou representante para se manifestar na audiência. Embora tenha integrado o grupo de clubes que se posicionaram publicamente contra a MP, alegando prejuízos financeiros aos orçamentos das equipes, o time alvinegro não participou das sustentações orais realizadas perante o ministro Luiz Fux.
Durante a audiência, representantes de clubes e entidades esportivas argumentaram que os contratos de patrocínio foram firmados com base na legislação vigente à época e que a proibição compromete receitas previamente planejadas. Outro ponto de contestação foi o prazo de dez dias estabelecido para a adaptação ao novo modelo.
As manifestações dos dirigentes esportivos, no entanto, contrastaram com os argumentos apresentados pelo governo federal, que defende a manutenção da proibição diante dos impactos das apostas sobre o endividamento das famílias e a saúde pública.
Governo aponta aumento na procura por atendimento no SUS
O ministro da Saúde, Alexandre Padilha, defendeu a manutenção da medida e alertou para as consequências da dependência em jogos online. Durante sua participação, destacou os riscos de endividamento, violência familiar, agravamento de problemas de saúde mental e suicídios relacionados ao vício em apostas.
“A única e melhor solução para evitar suicídios, evitar pessoas viciadas, violência familiar, é mantermos a proibição das bets”, afirmou.
Padilha apresentou dados que apontam um aumento de 200% na procura por atendimento no Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) em decorrência de problemas associados às apostas. Segundo o ministro, 28 milhões de pessoas fizeram apostas nos 12 meses anteriores à proibição. Desse total, aproximadamente 11 milhões apresentaram padrões de risco ou comportamento problemático.
Outro dado apresentado foi o registro de 1,2 milhão de pedidos de autoexclusão de CPFs, mecanismo que permite bloquear o acesso dos usuários às plataformas de apostas.
“Não é dinheiro que se perde, perde o controle da vida. Quarenta por cento deles [do total de 1,2 milhão] falaram que não aguentam mais perder o controle”, acrescentou.
O ministro também argumentou que a experiência internacional demonstra o agravamento dos indicadores de saúde relacionados aos jogos online em países que legalizaram as apostas. Para ele, a proibição é uma medida necessária para evitar que os prejuízos sejam transferidos para o sistema público de saúde e para as famílias.
Proibição também mobiliza movimentos sociais
A discussão no STF ocorre em meio a uma mobilização de movimentos sociais e organizações da sociedade civil pela manutenção da proibição. Na noite de segunda-feira (2), o Instituto Conhecimento Liberta (ICL), liderado pelo educador e empresário Eduardo Moreira, lançou a campanha “Bets Nunca Mais”.
O abaixo-assinado, que ultrapassou 1,5 milhão de assinaturas em menos de 24 horas, reúne três reivindicações centrais: a manutenção da proibição das apostas, o fim da publicidade e dos patrocínios de empresas do setor em clubes esportivos e transmissões de jogos, além da ampliação do atendimento público às pessoas afetadas pela ludopatia e às famílias endividadas.
A mobilização busca pressionar o Supremo a manter a validade da MP nº 1.394/2026, editada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em 25 de setembro. A medida é questionada pela Associação Nacional de Jogos e Loterias, que acionou a Corte para tentar restabelecer as operações das plataformas e a publicidade do setor.
:: Relembre: Governo Lula anuncia Medida Provisória que determina o fim das bets no Brasil ::
O STF analisa a Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade (ADI) 8027, apresentada por entidades ligadas ao mercado de apostas, que alegam insegurança jurídica e prejuízos aos contratos comerciais firmados antes da proibição.
Debate sobre patrocínios gera repercussão
Uma das manifestações que provocaram reação nas redes sociais foi a do presidente do Fluminense, Matheus Montenegro. Durante a audiência, o dirigente comparou os impactos do endividamento das famílias aos possíveis prejuízos financeiros provocados pela proibição das bets para os clubes.
Montenegro argumentou que a interrupção dos contratos poderia provocar uma redução significativa nas receitas das equipes, com consequências como demissões de funcionários. A comparação foi criticada por integrantes da sociedade civil, que apontaram a diferença entre os prejuízos financeiros enfrentados por instituições esportivas e os danos sociais provocados pelo endividamento de famílias por causa das apostas.
Os dados sobre o impacto econômico das plataformas ajudam a dimensionar o problema. De acordo com informações do Boletim Fiscal dos Estados, as famílias brasileiras perderam R$ 62,5 bilhões em apostas no ano passado.
Além dos prejuízos individuais, o governo aponta que a expansão do mercado de apostas comprometeu parte da renda destinada ao consumo e às necessidades básicas. O Brasil chegou a registrar cerca de 50 milhões de usuários dessas plataformas, com mais de 80 empresas atuando no mercado antes da proibição.
Supermercados registram aumento nas vendas
Os possíveis efeitos econômicos da proibição também aparecem nos indicadores do varejo alimentar. Levantamento da Associação Brasileira de Supermercados (Abras) apontou crescimento de 6,5% nas vendas do setor entre 5 e 11 de outubro, na comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior. Na semana seguinte, entre 12 e 18 de outubro, a alta foi de 6,3%.
Em Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo e no interior do Rio de Janeiro, o crescimento chegou a 10,6%, segundo os dados apresentados. Entre os produtos que impulsionaram o resultado estão itens de primeira necessidade, como arroz, óleo, macarrão e café.
:: Leia também: Consumo de alimentos cresce após proibição das bets no país, diz Abras ::
O movimento foi apontado como um possível reflexo da redução dos gastos das famílias com apostas, permitindo que parte da renda voltasse a ser destinada ao consumo cotidiano. Dados relacionados às transferências via Pix também indicaram queda nos pagamentos direcionados às plataformas após a proibição.
A rejeição às apostas online também aparece nas pesquisas de opinião. Levantamento Atlas/Bloomberg, divulgado em 23 de setembro, apontou que 75% dos brasileiros são favoráveis ao fim das plataformas.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘Um Nordeste sem estereótipos’: Lázaro Ramos reflete sobre a estreia de ‘Feito Pipa’ e a corrida ao Oscar
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Lucas Salum
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Escolhido para representar o Brasil no Oscar, “Feito Pipa” chega aos cinemas de todo país nesta quinta-feira (5), com Lázaro Ramos, Teca Pereira e o jovem ator revelação Yuri Gomes, de 11 anos, todos sob a regência do diretor cearense Allan Deberton.
Premiado como melhor ator coadjuvante no Festival de Gramado, Lázaro Ramos conversou com o Brasil de Fato sobre as expectativas da estreia e se demonstrou confiante para a busca pela mais prestigiada estatueta do cinema.
“Eu estou torcendo muito para que as pessoas vejam todas as temáticas que são tratadas ali. Ele tem uma grande qualidade, não é um filme didático, né? Por isso ele sensibiliza tanto”, comenta. “As pessoas mais sensíveis vão conseguir identificar as outras camadas. Mas quem não tiver sensibilidade a esses outros temas também desfrutará do filme.”
O longa se passa no interior do Ceará, em uma cidade que foi impactada pela construção de uma barragem. Gugu, interpretado por Yuri Gomes, é um menino de 11 anos que perdeu a mãe e é criado pela avó Dilma, personagem de Teca Pereira.
Lázaro Ramos é o pai que age de maneira ríspida com o menino e não respeita o jeito dele ser e se expressar.
“Temos um vilão e um herói, mas não com as tintas que geralmente pintam um herói ou um vilão. Eu acho que tem umas sutilezas aí, uns não ditos, uns olhares, umas opções de tom de cena que eu acho que deixam o filme muito interessante.”
Como pano de fundo, o filme revela como a construção de barragens impacta a saúde mental da população. Lázaro Ramos comenta que conhece essa realidade e que esse é um dos elementos que traz veracidade para o longa ao retratar um Nordeste “sem estereótipos”.
Confira a entrevista na íntegra
Brasil de Fato: Lázaro, o filme com certeza foge daquele maniqueísmo do bem contra o mal. Mas, na sua opinião, temos um herói e um vilão?
Lázaro Ramos: Temos um vilão e um herói, mas não com as tintas que geralmente pintam um herói ou um vilão. Eu acho que tem umas sutilezas aí, uns não ditos, uns olhares, umas opções de tom de cena que eu acho que deixam o filme muito interessante nesse lugar.
Eu acho que a opção desse herói [o personagem Gugu] é muito legal porque dá protagonismo a um personagem que, em outros filmes e situações, seria um coadjuvante, sem muita história.
Ele tem história, ele está pleno, ele está dizendo: “Eu sou assim”. Em nenhum momento ele se nega a ser quem ele é.
Ele não passa pelo momento do herói da dúvida, de “eu aceito o meu poder, ou não”. Ele sabe: “Eu sou poderoso, eu sou assim, você que está errado de não me aceitar do jeito que eu sou”. Então dá uma tinta diferente para esse herói.
E esse vilão [Batista, pai de Gugu], ao mesmo tempo, não é um vilão que parece estar distante da gente, que a gente aponta o dedo, “olha como esse homem é mau”. Ele está próximo da gente. Ele parece com a gente às vezes. Porque ele mostra que tem amor pelo filho, mas tem uma rigidez e uma incapacidade de aceitar o filho do jeito que é, o que o torna um vilão.
Não um vilão que está num lugar comum, mas um vilão que a gente diz assim: “Eu podia ser esse vilão porque às vezes eu quero controlar o jeito do outro existir, às vezes eu sou violento também, eu cometo essas pequenas violências em algum momento.”
Queria aproveitar que a gente está ainda respirando esse clima pós-eleição para trazer um assunto que dialoga com o filme: a terceira idade. A gente se emocionou muito vendo senhorzinhos e senhorinhas indo votar de cadeira de rodas, com cilindro de oxigênio, enfim… E o filme debate política de cuidado ao retratar a personagem Dilma, uma mulher idosa que quer viver. Você fez essa relação também?
Eu acho que, em vários sentidos, ela [Dilma, avô de Gugu], apesar de já ter uma certa idade, não perdeu os códigos de bem viver dela, de namorar, de gostar de ir para a festa, de ser desbocada com o neto dela.
Além disso, é exemplar o amor que o Gugu tem pela avó dele. Eu queria ter minha avó viva agora para exercer esse amor tão lindo que o Gugu nos lembra e nos ensina.
Nesse ano em que a gente viu a nossa terceira idade se mobilizando pelo país, dando sua opinião, indo votar, eu acho que é didático. Eu acho que o filme, sem ter mirado esse momento histórico, vem num bom momento para a gente abrir o nosso coração para esses temas todos.
Outro tema muito importante que o filme aborda é o da população atingida por barragem. É um assunto que foi novo para ti?
Não, não foi novo. Eu venho de uma cidade pequena também. Wagner [Moura], que é meu amigo, meu irmão, tem uma história da cidade dele ter sido toda inundada para a construção da barragem. Eu já visitei cidades que têm essa experiência.
Eu estou torcendo muito para que as pessoas vejam todas as temáticas que são tratadas ali [em “Feito Pipa”]. Ele tem uma grande qualidade, não é um filme didático, né? Por isso ele sensibiliza tanto.
As pessoas mais sensíveis vão conseguir identificar as outras camadas. Mas quem não tiver sensibilidade a esses outros temas também desfrutará do filme.
Agora, o tema da barragem, da inundação, da morte da mãe do Gugu estão ali como uma camada importantíssima para falar, inclusive, de uma região do Brasil que muitas vezes é estereotipada na sua representação.
É um Nordeste que não tem estereótipos. Esses personagens estão olhados com carinho e com respeito na sua ambiência em que vivem, naquela cidade, no jeito que é fotografada, no jeito que se vestem, no jeito que mostram o seu desejo, nas músicas que escutam, que é muito mais próximo do que é o nosso Nordeste, do que é o meu Nordeste, do que algumas vezes foi representado.
Queria falar de Oscar. Você está apegado à teoria do “Saneamento Básico”, que diz que os atores deste filme estão sendo todos indicados, que aconteceu com a Fernanda Torres e o Wagner Moura e que você seria o próximo?
Eu acho que é verdade. Eu já estou dizendo isso que é verdade, já estou chamando o Jorge Furtado de Nostradamus do cinema brasileiro. Acho que, depois de Fernanda Torres, Wagner e eu, ano que vem temos Tonico Pereira, Camila Pitanga em breve, Bruno Garcia. A lista está ali…
Uma última pergunta que foge um pouco do filme, mas não queria perder a oportunidade de perguntar: como você reagiu, qual foi a sensação de ser elogiado pelo Daniel Vorcaro?
[Risos] Eu fiquei tão feliz em ser chatinho. Eu fiquei muito feliz. É sinal de que a gente está fazendo certo, está tomando as decisões certas, né?

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: ‘Whitewater is ephemeral. That’s why we chase it’: Nouria Newman on the risk and thrill of extreme kayaking
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Andy Cochrane
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Just hours before Nouria Newman planned to put in on the Klinaklini River in north-western British Columbia, she checked the water gauge at the mouth of the river. The levels had looked good. Then it started raining.
Water flows doubled overnight, turning the Class V lower gorge into a death trap. Even in good conditions, the Klinaklini is one of the most elusive rivers in the world. Of the three groups that had attempted before her to paddle the full 125 miles to the Pacific, only one was successful. Newman, a French professional kayaker, was hoping to be the second.
After waiting for flows to recede, Newman and her paddling partner, Sandy MacEwan, launched on to the river. By the time they reached the 12-mile crux, the river had returned to its normal volume, around 10,000 cubic feet per second. Carefully scouting the six canyons that make up the lower gorge, they completed the second full descent.
“Rivers like this are exciting, scary and unknown,” Newman said. “Whitewater is ephemeral, that’s why we keep chasing it. A lot of people see happiness as a whole – family, job, house, money – but I see whitewater as these super, super happy moments, and then I move on to the next thing.”
The 35-year-old is one of the most accomplished kayakers in the world, largely because of her ability to see a river for what it is: an ever-changing canvas that oscillates quickly between ecstasy and catastrophe. Newman’s early career was defined by competitions, both slalom and freestyle. In 2013 she won the Ottawa XL, one of the biggest freestyle events in the world, and took second at the ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships. In 2014 she won gold at the world championships in the team category. She has been named an extreme kayaking world champion five times. Yet, despite her success paddling gates and doing tricks in controlled environments, Newman was drawn to wild rivers.
The seed was planted on an impromptu trip to the Stikine River, where she became the first woman to run Site Zed, one of the most dangerous rapids in the world. “I bought a ticket the day before and didn’t go thinking I was going to run Site Zed,” Newman said, “but when we scouted it, I felt good about the line. I’ve learned to trust that feeling.”
Running the Stikine, which flows from northern British Columbia to southern Alaska, brought a lot of attention, something that helped Newman pivot further towards remote rivers around the world. Over the last decade she’s paddled in dozens of countries including solo expeditions in India and Madagascar and first descents in Colombia and China. She set the world record for the largest waterfall drop by a woman at 104ft, and was the first woman to run the Rondu Gorge in Pakistan in 2023.
With these accolades it’s easy to assume Newman is nearly fearless. The truth is more complex.
Growing up in Le Villaret du Nial, a village in the French Alps, Newman had access to rivers, mountains, and the outdoors. At the age of five, she took her first kayaking class with a local club, which pushed her towards competitions because they relied on results for funding.
At six, she paddled her first wild river, the Chéran, which includes a particularly steep access where the boats and gear had to be lowered down with ropes. “I loved that feeling of adventure,” Newman said, “but I was too slow so my dad clipped me on to his boat and towed me fast, so I flipped upside down. I was hitting rocks, scared, cold, crying and angry at my dad. Then we stopped and had a picnic, and I was happy again. I learned you can’t kayak without being cold at some point.”
She won her first race when she was eight, and was recruited by the national federation training center at 15, but decided to stay with her club. During high school she would paddle every day before or after class, and even sometimes at lunchtime. After graduating she moved to Toulouse in southern France to study at Sciences Po, a prestigious university.
At the same time she earned one of three spots on the French slalom team, but only one athlete could go to the Olympics. “Everyone was fighting for the spot,” she said. “Mentors who had been nice to me since I was young suddenly changed how they treated me. The atmosphere was really bad.”
Tensions between Newman and the federation grew, largely because of politics outside paddling. “I was raised in a way where I didn’t assume all adults are right,” said Newman. “The federation told me to study sports science, but I wasn’t interested. I wanted something outside of sports, so I wasn’t focused on it all the time. That created some issues.” On weekends she took trips to paddle whitewater, a rarity in a slalom world defined by precision and predictability – another decision the federation disliked.
Although Sciences Po was just 20 minutes from the training facility, Newman often had to miss training sessions because of class. When the federation scheduled a training camp the week before her exams, she skipped it so she wouldn’t fail. School remained her priority. In 2018 she graduated with a master’s degree in journalism and political science and a focus on sociology. Her thesis was on social constructs and fear – specifically how women are conditioned from a young age to be more fearful than men.
At the end of 2017, after shoulder surgery and two seasons of up-and-down results, Newman was kicked off the federation team. Feeling lost, she flew to India for a solo expedition on the Tsarap, Zanskar and Indus Rivers, sometimes called the Grand Canyon of Asia. With her mind in a fog, she underestimated a line and her boat was pinned on a rock above a siphon, one of the most dangerous features in a river.
After four minutes of trying to free her boat with her head barely above water, Newman pulled her skirt and tried to climb up the rocks, but the water sucked her into the siphon. Fortunately, she flushed through safely. In shock but without options, Newman paddled for five more days to reach the river’s end. Such close calls have taught her about risk, the unknown and decision making.
“In the prep, risk is rational, it’s a calculation. On the river it has to be more intuitive,” said Newman, who admits that her calculations aren’t always right. “If you do this long enough, you see the contradiction. You want to bring the risk lower, but you’re willing to test it. It’s like having little demons that try to push it too far. We’re humans, so we will make mistakes at some point.”
Most people, Newman believes, don’t understand the difference between risk and consequence. “Risk is the odds you’re going to miss the line. Consequence is what happens if you do. Alex Honnold is a great example. What he does has extremely high consequences, but the risk that he falls is very, very low.”
One of the most difficult tasks is explaining decisions to her parents. Newman used to lie to her mother about waterfalls, but doesn’t any more. “They now know more than they sometimes want to, even if they don’t always understand why I do it,” Newman said. “My why is always changing. Whitewater pulls you toward a river, but what you remember is the people you were with, not the whitewater.”
Like most paddlers on the sharp end of the sport, Newman has had her fair share of close calls. On the Clearwater River in Canada she lost focus and was pushed into a recirculating water trap. “I was arrogant and not respecting the river, and got beat down,” she said.
Newman believes that most of kayaking, at least at her level, is in your own head, balancing fear, goals and ego. These lessons translate well to the rest of life. “In my exams at university I sat next to this girl who was so stressed. Worst case she fails and takes the class again, so why feel that bad?” Still, there are a few everyday things in everyday life that give Newman anxiety, like doing taxes, driving in traffic, or parallel parking in a tight spot, because she hasn’t pushed the limits on them.
Despite being a writer, expedition planner and entrepreneur, Newman wants only to be known as a whitewater kayaker. “Everyone these days calls themselves an adventurer or influencer or explorer. I don’t know what that means any more,” said Newman. “Climbing an 8,000m peak with fixed ropes is not a real adventure, there is no unknown. You’re not even an alpinist. If you run the Grand Canyon with an outfitter, it’s not whitewater. These words are so common they mean nothing, so I don’t use them.”
This directness is what makes Newman stand out. She’s never been afraid to share what’s on her mind, to the French kayaking federation, the media or anyone else. She learned how to be direct on river trips, which remain the most important thing in her life.
“I would buy a plane ticket for tomorrow to try a new river. My business model is to put kayaking first, and then everything else,” said Newman. “I don’t want YouTube or Instagram to take too much time. I could make more if I followed the algorithm, but that would take away from me kayaking. Other people might get an agent or a sunscreen ad or be on a billboard, but I don’t care about that. I do it my way.”

https://taz.de/Vorwuerfe-gegen-Oezdemir-.title: Vorwürfe gegen Özdemir-Berater: War Palmer übergriffig?
https://taz.de/Vorwuerfe-gegen-Oezdemir-.author: Benno Stieber
https://taz.de/Vorwuerfe-gegen-Oezdemir-.text:
Vorwürfe gegen Özdemir-Berater: War Palmer übergriffig?
Eine ehemalige Stadträtin wirft dem Tübinger Oberbürgermeister einen sexuellen Übergriff vor. Boris Palmer dementiert, lässt aber seinen Nebenjob ruhen.
Wieder Ärger um Boris Palmer: Eine ehemalige Tübinger Gemeinderätin von „Die Partei“ wirft dem Tübinger Oberbürgermeister mindestens einen sexuellen Übergriff vor. Konkret soll er nach ihrer Darstellung nach ersten einvernehmlichen intimen Zusammentreffen gegen ihren erklärten Willen ihre Brüste angefasst haben. Palmer weist die Vorwürfe zurück.
Auch wenn bisher nicht klar ist, was wirklich vorgefallen ist und Palmer rechtliche Schritte prüft: An ihm und seinen ehemaligen Grünen-Parteifreunden werden diese Anschuldigungen nicht ohne Blessur vorübergehen. Geben sie doch all jenen recht, die Palmer immer schon für ein unkalkulierbares Risiko gehalten haben.
Linken war er mit seinen Positionen zu Political Correctness und Genderthemen immer ein rotes Tuch. Satirisch gemeinte oder tatsächliche rassistische Äußerungen jenseits jeder Geschmacksgrenze gefährdeten den Bundestagswahlkampf von Annalena Baerbock. Erneute Äußerungen dieser Art und Nazi-Verharmlosungen beendeten dann seine politische Karriere bei den Grünen. Er trat aus, um weiteren Schaden von der Partei abzuwenden.
Cem Özdemir, Ministerpräsident von Baden-Württemberg und langjähriger Freund Palmers, sorgte im Frühjahr für erste Wiederannäherungen mit einem Comeback. Er setzte ihn gezielt im Wahlkampf für konservative männliche Wähler ein, ließ sich sogar von ihm verheiraten. Nach der Wahl machte ihn Özdemir zum Berater für Entbürokratisierung.
Eine andere Dimension
Aber diesmal geht es nicht um Worte, sondern einen Tatvorwurf. Die ehemalige Gemeinderätin will ein, wie sie es nennt, „geheim gehaltenes sexuell aufgeladenes Verhältnis“ mit Palmer gehabt haben, in dem es zu einem Übergriff gekommen sein soll. Auf Instagram hatte die Frau öffentlich persönliche Fotos und Auszüge aus undatierten WhatsApp-Chats mit Palmer veröffentlicht und eine 17-seitige Erklärung abgegeben.
Darin berichtet die ehemalige Stadträtin äußerst detailliert über die nach ihrer Darstellung zeitweise intime Beziehung zu Palmer, die nach ihrem Ausscheiden aus dem Gemeinderat begonnen habe. Sie berichtet auch offen über Missbrauchserfahrungen, psychische Probleme und Suizidversuche, von denen Palmer gewusst habe.
Palmer entgegnete in einer schriftlichen Stellungnahme nach der Veröffentlichung des Textes am Dienstag: „Die Vorwürfe sind haltlos. Ich werde mich hiergegen zur Wehr setzen und lasse rechtliche Schritte prüfen.“
Resozialisierung auf der Kippe
Schon in der Vergangenheit war dem Tübinger OB eine private Beziehung öffentlich in die Quere gekommen. Im Herbst 2022, vor seiner zweiten Wiederwahl, war eine Bewerberin für einen Job in Palmers Sekretariat vor Gericht gezogen. Die Frau gab an, wegen einer früheren Liaison mit dem OB nicht zum Zuge gekommen zu sein. Die Klage wurde jedoch abgewiesen.
Nach dem letzten Ausfall Palmers 2023, der zu seinem Austritt bei den Grünen geführt hatte, nahm sich der Kommunalpolitiker eine Auszeit und die Dienste eines Coaches in Anspruch. Palmers Beraterjob zum Bürokratieabbau, den er jetzt ruhen lässt, sollte eigentlich Teil einer Art Resozialisierung des Enfant terrible mit der grünen Partei sein. Die könnte nun dauerhaft gescheitert sein. Nach der Veröffentlichung der aktuellen Vorwürfe erklärt Palmer: „Ich habe gegenüber dem Ministerpräsidenten erklärt, dass ich mein Ehrenamt für Staatsmodernisierung und Verwaltungsvereinfachung ruhen lasse, bis die Vorwürfe aufgeklärt sind.“
Özdemir soll Palmer darum gebeten haben, hört man aus dem Staatsministerium. Diesmal ist ein Comeback ungewiss.Gegenüber der taz hatte Özdemir im Sommer zur Zuverlässigkeit seines Freundes Palmer gesagt: „Ich habe ihm klar gesagt: Es ist auch für dich eine Chance, dein Verhältnis zu den Grünen zu korrigieren. Ich würde mich sehr darüber freuen, wenn es passiert. Aber das habe ich nicht allein in der Hand.“

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Resounding wins for Democrats a wholesale rebuke of Trump’s Maga movement
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Rachel Leingang in Des Moines
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
No single Democratic coalition can claim victory after Tuesday’s resounding midterm results – all parts of the Democratic coalition can.
Their wins were so sweeping, so resounding, that factional divisions fail to explain them. This year, the most important thing Democrats had to be to win was, simply, not Republicans.
Trump gave Democrats the political gifts of a deeply unpopular war against Iran that led to rising prices, chaotic tariffs that devastated small businesses, farmers and international alliances, healthcare cuts, a deadly deportation scheme, self-enrichment, corruption, a never-ending debacle over a reflecting pool renovation.
Democrats took the ball and ran with it, taking on Trump as popularity continued to slide. It wasn’t just the typical midterm backlash a sitting president’s party faces; it was a wholesale rebuke of the president’s Make America Great Again movement, the clearest sign yet that voters have had enough of Trumpism.
Democrats of all stripes declared victory on Tuesday night: moderates, progressives, populists, Democratic socialists. And they won up and down the ballot, flipping both chambers of Congress, several governor’s mansions and delivering multiple new legislative trifectas in the states. These victories will provide avenues for Democrats to hold Trump accountable and act as a functioning branch of government, something voters have said they’ve been missing in Trump 2.0.
Democrats competed deep in Republican strongholds – places that wouldn’t have made the map even six months ago. US senators will join Democratic ranks from Kansas and South Carolina. Texas went blue, and not just in one race. Voters in rural districts that Democrats had previously written off showed they could be persuaded. Maine voters ousted a 30-year veteran of the US Senate despite a scandal-plagued Democratic candidate, who was eventually replaced.
At the Democratic watch party in Des Moines, Iowa, where Democrats flipped the governor’s office, US Senate and three of four congressional districts, the excitement neared a level of disbelief.
“To Iowa Democrats, we’ve had a hard few years here in Iowa, but balanced government has been restored,” Rob Sand, elected the state’s next governor, told supporters in his victory remarks.
These wins will give Democrats a chance to hold Trump accountable at all levels of government – and to prove to voters that they can competently govern, should they harness the momentum.
The depth of the Democratic wins underscore the unpopularity of the Republicans, something voters around the country have been signaling all year. In talking to voters over this past year, I felt their deep discontent, an anger that animated their votes, on a level I hadn’t seen before. On the campaign trail, voters of all political stripes were fed up, their fury at the status quo rose above all else on their list of voting priorities.
When I asked progressive political consultant Anat Shenker-Osorio about this months ago, she predicted that the midterms would be decided by the “mad as hell, ain’t going to take it any more” vote, as midterms often are. It would not be a sudden embrace of Democrats, but a “plague on both your houses”, she said. The size of Democrats’ wave would depend on how persuasive they were at convincing angry and disillusioned voters to turn out.
Given the blue tsunami, it seems they were convinced their vote was worth it.
In most instances, Democratic candidates showed up and listened. They held town halls all over their districts, hearing the anger that punctuated politics. The Democrats raged vertically, at the billionaires and elites who rule the US political system, blaming them for rising income inequality that leaves Americans feeling like it’s impossible to get ahead.
Voters, the results showed, are done with Trump’s Republican party. Trump’s coalition has all but driven out any remaining factions that publicly disagreed with the president. The Republicans, now, need to contend with what they will become after Trump.
Could there have been a lane for Republicans who explicitly ran against the Trump agenda, saying they would work to rein in the executive and hold him accountable? We don’t know. No one really tried.
The attempts at fearmongering – over trans people, or Arab Americans, or Hasan Piker – didn’t work. The fundamentals of Americans’ lives were worse. It was Republicans’ fault, voters decided.
They paid far more for gas because of a war they didn’t support. They dropped their healthcare because they couldn’t afford it after Congress allowed subsidies to expire. They watched as data centers moved into their towns, a physical manifestation of the disruption artificial intelligence could bring to their lives. Trump dismissed their concerns over these issues, claiming they essentially weren’t happening, or were a necessary step toward greater goals. Voters even rebelled against Republican attempts to gerrymander seats more favorable to their party, with major defeats in seats that the party should have easily carried by double digits.
Trump repeatedly told voters to pretend he was on the ballot, believing it would rally his base and help stave off huge losses for Republicans. But, as some voters said today, his presence was clear – and it backfired. In Rochester, New Hampshire, independent voter Rebecca Connors said she voted for Democrats to send a message to Trump that “he’s wreaking havoc”.
“All across the state and all across this country, people are saying, ‘Enough is enough,’” Minnesota Democratic US senator-elect Peggy Flanagan said after her victory. “You just beat Donald Trump. America did too.”
Though eyes will quickly shift toward 2028, Democrats now have an opportunity to seize the power voters have entrusted them with and use it to rebuild their party. The Republicans, though, have even more soul-searching to do, with the midterm results fresh in the rearview mirror.

https://taz.de/Kampagne-gegen-Linke/!622.title: Kampagne gegen Linke: Die neue Maßlosigkeit
https://taz.de/Kampagne-gegen-Linke/!622.author: Charlotte Wiedemann
https://taz.de/Kampagne-gegen-Linke/!622.text:
Kampagne gegen Linke: Die neue Maßlosigkeit
Von Paris bis Berlin: Mit Polizeigewalt und medialer Propaganda soll das Vertrauen in eine Alternative und die eigene Handlungsmacht zerstört werden.
E s schien, als zerfalle der Rechtsstaat wie im Zeitraffer, just vor meinen Augen. In einem Land, das nicht das eigene ist und dessen Zustände man nicht tagtäglich beobachtet, analysiert und sortiert, bekommen dramatische Momente eine besondere Verdichtung, es ist die Wucht verdichteter Zeitgeschichte, und sie traf mich in Paris wie ein Schlag.
Nächtliche Ausgangssperren. Eine Landkarte mit einem Netz von Demonstrationsverboten. Tausende Festnahmen Minderjähriger, manche in kalten Zellen interniert, ohne Matratze, Decke, Essen. Vor allem aber die Polizei: Sie tritt auf, als herrsche sie über koloniale Subjekte, die sie jederzeit demütigen darf, mit Schlägen, Kontrollen, Gummigeschossen.
So schrankenlos und zugleich so institutionalisiert ist diese Gewalt, dass man kaum zu glauben vermag, sie stünde im Dienst eines demokratischen Staates. Maßlos – das Wort verließ mich nicht mehr.
ist Autorin in Berlin, viele Jahre mit dem Schwerpunkt Islamische Lebenswelten. Zuletzt erschien „Den Schmerz der Anderen begreifen. Holocaust und Weltgedächtnis“ (Propyläen).
Manchmal sangen Demonstranten die Marseillaise, wenn die Polizei auf sie zustürmte. Sie reklamierten die Revolutionsgeschichte, reklamierten die Republik für ihren Protest und ihren Antifaschismus. Die Musiker des 200-köpfigen „Orchestre du Noveau Monde“ spielten im Tränengasnebel und trommelten den Rhythmus von „Siamo tutti antifascisti“ auf die Klangkörper ihrer Streichinstrumente. Es ist diese Dringlichkeit, die so sehr kontrastiert zur Larmoyanz der Oberklasse.
taz debatte
Die taz ist eine unabhängige, linke und meinungsstarke Tageszeitung. In unseren Kommentaren, Essays und Debattentexten streiten wir seit der Gründung der taz im Jahr 1979. Oft können und wollen wir uns nicht auf eine Meinung einigen. Deshalb finden sich hier teils komplett gegenläufige Positionen – allesamt Teil des sehr breiten linken Meinungsspektrums.
Medien im apokalyptischen Delirium
Das Frankreich der oberen Schichten verdammt die Linke und arrangiert sich mit den Rechtsextremen. Vor die Wahl gestellt, sich stärker besteuern zu lassen, um den Verfall des Landes aufzuhalten, oder mit Faschisten zu paktieren, scheint die Entscheidung gefallen. Über eine Präsidentin Marine Le Pen wird geredet wie über ein fait accompli. Schon tritt die Chefin der europäischen Zentralbank vorzeitig zurück, damit über ihre Nachfolge noch Macron mitentscheidet statt Le Pen. Die Dinge regeln sich.
Jordan Bardella, soeben als Chef des Rassemblement National wiedergewählt, hat es nicht geschadet, dass seine früheren antisemitischen Schriften bekannt wurden. Aufmunternd rief Netanjahu herüber, ein rechtsextrem regiertes Frankreich sei gut für Israel – denn jetzt demonstriere in den Straßen von Paris die Hamas, „der gemeinsame Feind“.
Netanjahu ist für maßlose Vergleiche bekannt, aber was trennt seinen wohlkalkulierten Wahnwitz von dem apokalyptischen Delirium, in das sich Spiegel-Redakteure hineinschrieben, als sie für eine eilig hochgejazzte Titelstory gegen die Linke Berlin zum Eldorado der Gewalt machten?
Flood Berlin with Shit
Wir kennen die Maßlosigkeit aus dem Trumpismus, die Überwältigungsstrategie Flood the Zone with Shit. Früher habe ich diese Methode nicht wirklich verstanden, doch seit der Berlin-Wahl weiß ich, wie es sich lebt in einer solchen Zone. Berlin ist ein Testfeld: ob in einer zunehmend hysterischen Atmosphäre ein links-soziales Projekt möglich ist; ob es eine Alternative zur Faschisierung gibt und wie weit die rechte Instrumentalisierung des Kampfes gegen Antisemitismus gehen kann.
In dieser Shit-Zone watest du durch einen Sumpf aus Propaganda, kommst kaum nach mit dem Erklären und Aufklären, und wenn du ein Bein aus dem Morast ziehen möchtest, ist es, als bliebe dein Schuh darin stecken. So entsteht (und das ist gewollt) das Bedürfnis, sich abzuwenden, ins Private zu flüchten.
Ein Paris-Besuch versprach Abstand, stattdessen wurde mir dort ein Muster von Gemeinsamkeiten klar. Die maßlose Gewalt der Polizei soll, wie die maßlose Verzerrung rechtsdrehender Medien (und anderer Akteure), das Vertrauen in eine Alternative zerstören, soll uns die Vernunft rauben und den Glauben an die eigene Handlungsmacht.
Methoden, die man früher nur von Bild kannte, sind bei vormaligen Qualitätsmedien gelandet. Heinrich Bölls Katharina Blum (Jüngere, bitte googeln!) heißt heute Elif Eralp. Und immer drängt jemand nach mit dem nächsten Tabubruch: Die Welt stellt das Fascho-Plädoyer für Remigration auf ihre Seite eins; die Berliner Junge Union will die Bundeswehr gegen Jugendproteste einsetzen. Und die Linke will, ja sicher, „jüdische Immobilienbesitzer“ enteignen.
Jede hanebüchene Anschuldigung ist erlaubt, wenn sie auf das nun allseits festgeschriebene Feindbild zielt: linksextrem + migrantisch + palästinensisch = antisemitisch. Kaum anders in Frankreich, wo ein Verbot der Linkspartei La France insoumise im Gespräch ist.
Dem Maßlosen nicht die Hand reichen
Aber die Maßlosigkeit zerfrisst ja auch die bürgerliche Demokratie von innen. In Paris eine Ausgangssperre ausgerechnet für die Place de la Bastille, welch traurige Ironie. Als würde sich damit die Republik nicht selbst beschädigen. Und natürlich hat der Spiegel nicht nur andere beschädigt, sondern auch sich selbst.
Wie bewahrt man in diesem Klima die eigene geistige Gesundheit? Was ist Widerstand, wenn die meisten von uns keine Aktivistinnen sind, sondern allenfalls engagierte Bürgerinnen? Dem Maßlosen nicht die Hand reichen und nicht den kleinen Finger. Süffige Feindbilder zurückweisen, denn immer beginnt es mit dem Süffigem. Widerstehen bedeutet, in einer Sprache zu denken und zu reden, die Verzweiflung ausdrücken kann, ohne zu demoralisieren, und die eine brennende Dringlichkeit vermittelt, ohne Zaghafte zu verschrecken.
Egal wie die Midterm-Wahlen in den USA ausgehen, Trumpismus minus Personenkult und Extrem-Narzissmus ist längst unter uns. Was vor einigen Jahren bizarr erschien, fern und fremd und für manche gar ulkig, ist heute die Shit-Zone vor unserer Haustür. Und die Muster sind stets ähnlich. Auch Zohran Mamdani in New York sollte durch bodenlose Vorwürfe, in deren Mittelpunkt Antisemitismus stand, schon vor dem Start die Legitimation entzogen werden. Er überstand diese Phase dank eines klugen Teams, über das die Berliner Linkspartei ganz offensichtlich nicht verfügt.

Wahlen in den USA: Der ranghöchste Demokrat der USA
Hakeem Jeffries wird Sprecher des Repräsentantenhauses und jubelt. Doch er muss mit Gegenwind aus dem Weißen Haus und aus seinen eigenen Reihen rechnen.
Der Demokrat Hakeem Jeffries hatte ein gelöstes Lachen auf dem Gesicht, als er kurz nach 23 Uhr in Washington vor seine Anhänger trat. Der ansonsten eher reservierte Abgeordnete aus New York genoss sichtlich den minutenlangen Jubel und reckte energisch wie zu seinen Football-Zeiten die Fäuste in die Luft.
Seine anschließende Rede fiel ebenso uncharakteristisch kräftig aus. „Die Menschen heute haben gezeigt, dass sie die Nase voll haben vom Extremismus und der Korruption in Washington.“ Dann gelobte er, für alle Amerikaner zu kämpfen, urbane und ländliche, schwarze, braune und weiße, konservative und progressive.
Jeffries wird in den kommenden zwei Jahren an vorderster Front dieses Kampfes stehen. Der bisherige Minderheitensprecher wird Sprecher des Abgeordnetenhauses und somit ranghöchster Demokrat der USA. Sollten Präsident und Vizepräsident durch ein Unglück ihr Amt nicht ausüben können, würde er ins Weiße Haus einziehen.
Der Posten ist der bisherige Höhepunkt und das lang gehegte Ziel von Jeffries’ Karriere. Als im Jahr 2018 Alexandria Ocasio Cortez ihren Gegner in der eigenen Partei, Jim Crowley, besiegte, sah Jeffries seine Chance. Eigentlich hätte Crowley Nachfolger von Nancy Pelosi werden sollen, der alten Dame im Kapitol, die 20 Jahre lang entweder Sprecherin des Hauses oder der Fraktion war. So aber gab es da eine Vakanz, in die Jeffries reinstoßen konnte.
Wie mit einem feindseligen Weißen Haus zurechtkommen?
Es dürfte jedoch in den kommenden Monaten Momente geben, in denen Jeffries seinen Wunsch verflucht, auf diesem Stuhl zu sitzen. Jeffries muss nicht nur einen Weg finden, mit einem feindseligen Weißen Haus zurechtzukommen, das vermutlich mit allen Mitteln die Arbeit des Kongresses sabotieren wird. Der 56-Jährige aus Brooklyn hat auch in der eigenen Partei keinen leichten Stand.
Die Wahl an diesem Dienstag hat einen Generationswechsel in der demokratischen Partei zementiert, der sich schon lange anbahnt. Die neuen Stars der Partei, James Talarico, Abdul El-Sayed, AOC oder Jon Ossoff sind allesamt Millenials. Das bringt Jeffries in eine komplizierte Lage. Als er 2023 nach Washington kam, verkörperte er Rebellion, Jugend und Aufbruch. Sein Spitzname war „Brooklyn Barack.“ Jetzt verkörpert er jedoch für die neue Generation und insbesondere für den sozialistischen Block das Establishment.
Der Ruf hat sich in den vergangenen zwei Jahren gefestigt. Die neue Garde wirft ihm vor, sich nicht energisch genug gegen die Trump-Regierung gestemmt zu haben. Er hat sich zwar vor laufenden Kameras zu einem lauten „Fuck Trump“ hinreißen lassen. Er hat sich, so lange es ging, gegen Trumps Haushalt gestemmt und dafür starkgemacht, dass der Kongress den Krieg gegen den Iran verfassungsgemäß ratifizieren muss. Dennoch glauben viele unter den Millenials in Washington, dass er zu zahm, zu diplomatisch, zu sehr vom Parlamentsalltag abgestumpft sei, um Trump effektiv die Stirn zu bieten.
Die Antipathie berührt zumindest in Teilen auf Gegenseitigkeit. Ein großer Fan der demokratischen Sozialisten war Jeffries noch nie. Er brachte sie immer mit den verzogenen jungen Weißen in Verbindung, die seine Hood in Brooklyn gentrifiziert haben. Mit seiner Unterstützung für Mamdani zögerte er bis zum allerletzten Augenblick. Und bei einem der wichtigsten Themen dieses Wahlkampfes, Israel, war er sich lange uneins mit der neuen Riege.
Anpassung an den Israel-Zeitgeist
Jeffries war Zeit seiner Karriere ein unerschütterlicher Unterstützer Israels, so sehr, dass man ihm in Anspielung an die Israel-freundliche Lobbygruppe AIPAC den Spitznamen „Aipac Shakur“ verpasste. Seine Sympathien für Israel hat er zwar nicht aufgegeben. Als Zugeständnis an den neuen Zeitgeist ist er nun jedoch mit der jüdischen Organisation J Street verbandelt, die sich für eine Zweistaatenlösung einsetzt.
So fällt Jeffries in den kommenden Jahren vor allem auch die Aufgabe zu, seine eigene Partei zu einen. Als Minderheiten-Sprecher ist ihm das dadurch gelungen, dass er mit jedem reden konnte, ob es nun Ocasio Cortez war oder Zentristen wie Josh Gottheimer aus New Jersey. Zu seinen besten Qualitäten gehört, dass er gut zuhören kann. „Doch irgendwann muss er auch einmal eine Marschroute vorgeben“, sagte ein anonymer Abgeordneter gegenüber dem New Yorker.
Die Marschroute, die er bei seiner Rede am Samstagabend vorgegeben hat, ist ein unermüdlicher Kampf gegen soziale Ungerechtigkeit und dafür, „dass sich jeder Bürger seinen amerikanischen Traum erfüllen kann.“ Große Sozialgesetze werden jedoch wohl am Veto Trumps scheitern. Dennoch kann das Haus sie formulieren und einbringen und damit eine Blaupause für 2028 zeichnen. Jeffries’ Leistung dabei wäre, seine Partei für eine gemeinsame Zukunft geeint zu haben und eine gemeinsame Vision zu entwickeln.
Darauf, dass er erneut ein Amtsenthebungsverfahren gegen Trump anstreben wird, mag er sich unterdessen bislang nicht festlegen. Dass das neue Repräsentantenhaus die Trump-Regierung unter Druck setzen wird, steht jedoch fest. Der Rechtsausschuss hat im vergangenen Jahr 130 Untersuchungen gegen die Trump-Regierung vorbereitet. Aus diesen Untersuchungen, zumeist wegen Korruption, könnten nun handfeste Klagen entstehen.
Es ist ein großes Paket an Aufgaben, die da auf Jeffries zukommen, und bis zu seinem Amtsantritt im Januar als Sprecher des neuen Parlaments ist es nicht mehr lange. Um die blaue Welle zu feiern, bleibt da kaum Zeit. Ab heute fängt die Arbeit an.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.title: Fenerbahce v Liverpool: Champions League – live
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.author: Simon Burnton
https://www.theguardian.com/football/liv.text:
45+1 mins: There’ll be one minute of stoppage time.
- Minute-by-minute updates on the early kick-off in Turkey
- Liverpool fizzle out against Arsenal | Email Simon
Wed 4 Nov 2026 13.33 EST
First published on Wed 4 Nov 2026 11.15 EST
Wed 4 Nov 2026 13.33 EST
First published on Wed 4 Nov 2026 11.15 EST
45 mins: Save! Lukaku plays Greenwood into space beyond Greenwood on the Fenerbahce left, and he stings Alisson’s palms with a shot.
43 mins: Lukaku beautifully sets up a teammate for a shooting chance at the edge of the D. Sadly the player he sets up is Kante, who isn’t much of a goalscorer.
41 mins: … and it’s headed to Yuksek, 30 yards out, whose shot misses the target by at least that distance.
41 mins: Fenerbahce win themselves a corner for the first time. Liverpool have had and wasted six.
39 mins: Fenerbahce are really troubling Liverpool at the moment. They zip the ball around the edge of the visitors’ box for a while before working it to Greenwood, whose shot goes just wide of the near post.
37 mins: Barcola’s header from Munoz’s left-wing cross bounces a foot or so wide.
35 mins: This is all very frantic. Iraola spoke yesterday about how his team needed “to try to kill the confidence and momentum they can have with the supporters”. They have not done that.
32 mins: Another chance for the Turks! This time Lukaku gets into the right side of the area but what follows is neither cross nor shot, and duly is a goal kick.
31 mins: It was not good defending from Jacquet, who jumped in the wall as if his priority was not preventing a goal but preventing himself getting hit, twisting to get himself side-on. The ball then skidded off his thigh, and past Alisson.
GOAL! Fenerbahce 1-1 Liverpool (Greenwood, 29 mins)
Another deflection, and another goal! This time it’s Mason Greenwood, from a free kick, whose shot was going well wide before it hit Jacquet.
28 mins: The Fenerbahce bench have not been greatly amused by the last few minutes, and Kuyt is booked for expressing his dissatisfaction.
27 mins: Now Fenerbahce hit the bar! A cross from the left, an outstretched leg in the centre, and the ball smashes into the woodwork!
GOAL! Fenerbahce 0-1 Liverpool (Nyoni, 25 mins)
A defensive header drops to the edge of the area, and Nyoni runs onto it and keeps his volley low, and when it deflects off Oppong Ederson is wrongfooted!
25 mins: It was a long, crossfield diagonal from the left. Greenwood took it under control really nicely, but Tsimikas got to him before he could shoot. Meanwhile …
24 mins: Willy Delajod, the VAR, appears not to have taken a closer look, and play continues.
23 mins: Nearly a goal for Fenerbahce! But Greenwood, as he swings his right foot, gets pushed from behind by Tsimikas and goes down! The referee waves play on, but the VAR might want to take a closer look.
21 mins: Close! Gomez crosses low from the right flank, but just too far in front of Barcola at the near post and the ball runs across goal and away to safety.
20 mins: Nearly a quarter of the way through the game and Liverpool have had 100% of the shots and 100% of the corners, as well as 75% of the passes. They’ve just had another corner, but not another shot.
17 mins: There is a whiff of away goal in the air here. Munoz gets into the area now, but his cross deflects behind off Yuksek.
16 mins: Save! Tsimikas underhits a backpass and Kante gets there before Alisson, but a) he shoots straight into the goalkeeper, and b) the referee had anyway given Liverpool a free-kick for a foul on Van Dijk by Lukaku.
15 mins: Liverpool, amid the whistles and boos, work the ball through midfield really well, but it ends up with Tsimikas who overhits his cross. Then moments later Tsimikas gets another chance, and this one is hit limply at Ederson.
13 mins: … from which he hits Victor Munoz, who was standing alongside the defensive wall.
12 mins: Ngumoha is brought down by Kante, not far outside the penalty area, and Szoboszlai will have a shot from the resulting free-kick.
9 mins: And barely a minute later Guendouzi gets lectured by the referee for having the cheek to question a free-kick decision, after Mac Allister went over in midfield (also not a free kick, mind).
7 mins: Nothing comes from the corner, and Munoz is sent running down the right for Liverpool. Guendouzi gets in front of him, and when Munoz briefly brushes a hand against him the Frenchman flings himself to the ground, and wins a free kick.
6 mins: Fenerbahce win an attacking throw-in, and out comes a towel so Brown can get a proper grip on it.
5 mins: And another one! From the corner Szoboszlai eventually sends in a good cross from the right, and Jacquet miscues a header from six yards! Goal kick.
4 mins: Chances! Tsimikas’s cross from the left bounces through to Munoz, who has an excellent shooting chance but his effort is mishit and therefore runs to Barcola, whose effort is even more miskicked, and the ball goes back to Munoz, who finally forces a save out of Ederson.
3 mins: They keep booing for another minute or so while Liverpool continue keeping that ball, but eventually Szoboszlai hits a pass out of play, and they stop for a bit.
2 mins: Whistles and boos as Liverpool play keep-ball for a bit.
1 min: Peeeeeep! Liverpool get the match under way.
Before kick-off, a minute’s silence in memory of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-pitch collision over the weekend.
The players are on the pitch! And while the tournament anthem rings out, the Fenerbahce midfielder Yuksek gives his mascot a fairly intense cheek massage.
The players are gathering in the tunnel, while outside rain continues to fall, and Gala’s Freed from Desire rings out.
Classic football image here.
Dirk Kuyt has also had a pre-match chat:
 I’m feeling well, looking forward to the game. It’s a bit of English weather, but for football it’s amazing. I feel the atmosphere is going to be amazing, so let’s go for it. Of course when you work very intensively for four months together with the head coach and his staff it’s never easy when there are changes. You’re always looking for stability. The main thing is to be united, to stay working hard and to be tied together. Liverpool have some pretty good memories about Liverpool and if you believe in yourself and the magic is in the air you never know what you can do. The first thing is we need to show energy on the pitch, we have to play physical. The main thing is if we show the energy on the pitch the crowd will get behind us and they will lift us up.
Andoni Iraola has a pre-match chat about his team changes:
 I think we’ve been doing it all season. If you play every three four days you need to refresh the legs. In defensive positions we don’t have so many options, but in attacking positions we can see other options. I think Bradley, even Victor, are wingers but have played sometimes up front and I think we should be mobile, able to attack spaces if they are there, have good combinations also outside. I think Bradley can do this job very well.
And on the atmosphere they’re set to face:
 We’ve tried to do all the mentality stuff. You are playing something different when you are playing a Turkish team. I hope we can be at the level because the beginning of their last Champions League game they scored two goals straight away. It would be a very important win, because it would put us in a very good position for the second half of this league phase.
The Liverpool players have arrived at the catchily-named Şükrü Saracoğlu Spor Kompleksi, where it is apparently very wet. Şükrü Saracoğlu, since you ask, was Turkish prime minister between 1942 and 1946, and also president of Fenerbahce from 1934 to 1950.
The teams!
The teams have been named, and here they jolly well are! Five changes for Liverpool, with Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak among those dropping to the bench and Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas among those hopping into the first XI.
Fenerbahce: Ederson, Nelson Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Brown, Guendouzi, Kante, Yuksek, Greenwood, Lukaku, Kahveci. Subs: Tarik Cetin, Gunok, Akturkoglu, Demir, Muldur, Muriqi, Mercan, Elmaz, Dorgeles, Aydin, Mimovic.
 
Liverpool: Alisson, Gomez, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas, Mac Allister, Nyoni, Munoz, Szoboszlai, Ngumoha, Barcola. Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Kerkez, Wirtz, Isak, Gakpo, Araujo, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Koumas.
 
Referee: Clement Turpin (France).
Earlier today Liverpool’s Under-19s beat their Fenerbahce counterparts 5-3, with Will Wright scoring a hat-trick. They were 3-1 up after just 20 minutes, and 4-2 up after half an hour, while Fenerbahce finished with 10 men after Ali Demirbilek was sent off in stoppage time. Also on the scoresheet was Finn Inglethorpe, son of Liverpool’s long-time academy director, Alex.
Here’s Andy Hunter’s pre-match missive from Istanbul:
 Andoni Iraola has said Liverpool must improve their attacking play but dismissed concerns over the contrast between his team’s output in the Premier League and Champions League.
Liverpool boast a 100% record in Europe this season and can take a significant step towards qualification for the knockout phase with victory away at Fenerbahce on Wednesday.
Iraola’s side failed to register a shot on target, according to Opta, during Sunday’s defeat by Arsenal, the first time Liverpool have drawn a blank in a Premier League home game since their records began in 2003-04. The Liverpool head coach believes the statistic did not reflect his team’s performance but admitted there is room for improvement.
Much more here:
Preamble
Yesterday afternoon former Liverpool striker Dirk Kuyt told the media how excited he was to be facing his former team as Fenerbahce’s interim manager. “As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me and, from that moment, you know it will be a special occasion,” he beamed. “Of course, tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we’re in, I’m not here for myself. I’m here for the club and that’s what is important, to show the fans who deserve much more, a reaction, positive energy and a good performance.”
Then, at 11.25pm local time last night, the Turkish side announced that former Newcastle midfielder Emre Belozoglu – veteran also of two spells at Fener as a player and one as interim manager in 2021 – was replacing Kuyt, and his special occasion was imperilled. In the cold light of a new day it looks like Emre won’t take over until after this game, at which point Kuyt will either return to the role of assistant he held under previous head coach Ismail Kartal, or leave the club.
Either way, this promises to be a raucous farewell/not farewell. Fenerbahce are having a stinker of a season, sixth in the Super Lig having lost their last two league games, most recently experiencing a Hallowe’en nightmare at home to Goztepe, but this gives them a probably welcome distraction. Let’s see what they do with it, shall we?

Israeli settlers seize eight homes in occupied West Bank village west of Jericho
Israeli settlers seized eight Palestinian homes on Wednesday in the village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, Wafa news reported.
Palestinian security sources told Wafa that the settlers, accompanied by their families, stormed the eight homes, which were empty at the time of the raid, and smashed their doors, remaining inside the property.
Israeli forces also stormed Jericho and its refugee camps on Wednesday evening, deploying military vehicles along the city’s streets, according to Wafa.
They also reported that Israeli soldiers raided the area surrounding the Thabet Thabet Governmental Hospital in Tulkarm, in the occupied West Bank, and ransacked the home of Mohammed Ibrahim Shahada, secretary of Fatah in Tulkarm refugee camp on Wednesday.

US Senate Democrat leader Chuck Schumer said on Wednesday that the Iran war "must end", adding that his party's incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to put pressure on the Trump administration to do so.
"This war must end. It must end," AFP reported that Schumer told journalists, noting that the "power of the purse" is "one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people."
This comes after Vice President JD Vance blamed the US war on Iran for the Republican party's failures during the midterm elections.

https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/sk.title: Skulptur Projekte Münster 2027 Announces 13 More Commissions by Artists Including Kapwani Kiwanga, Ali Cherri, and Nolan Oswald Dennis
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/sk.author: Maximilíano Durón
https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/sk.text:
Skulptur Projekte Münster has announced 13 additional artist commissions that will appear across the German city when its sixth edition opens next year.
Opening in June, this upcoming iteration marks the decennial public art exhibition’s 50th anniversary and will be the first one organized since the death of Skulptur Projekte cofounder Kasper König in 2024. The curatorial collective What, How & for Whom / WHW (consisting of Ivet Ćurlin, Nataša Ilić, and Sabina Sabolović) will serve as artistic director.
At the core of the exhibition will be the Peace of Westphalia, the 1648 treaty that ended the Thirty Years’ War and was partially negotiated in Münster. Since then, the city has adopted a motto of “peace through dialogue.” The curators contrast that history with “Münster’s involvement in Europe’s long history of violent combat” as well as plan to address the present moment of “a world shaped by wars and smouldering conflicts,” per a release.
“Informed by the history of Münster as ‘City of Westphalian Peace,’ the artists of Skulptur Projekte 2027 are developing their proposals in awareness of the violence of the present, considering the political decisions, historical global relations, and economic systems that have shaped it,” WHW said in a statement. “Against the ruptures and losses of recent years, the exhibition asks not only what art can show, but what it can hold. In times when cancellations, censorship, and withdrawal have constrained cultural work, Skulptur Projekte seeks to make room for voices to be heard, for losses to be mourned, for consolation, and for alternatives to be proposed.”
Among the newly announced commissions are ones by Ali Cherri, Kapwani Kiwanga, Nolan Oswald Dennis, and Kosen Ohtsubo. Cherri will create several large-scale sculptures for the garden of the Officers’ Casino, part of the Gremmendorf military barracks that were built by the Nazis and used by the British military until 2012. Kiwanga’s project will look at the “ambiguous force of water,” from its nourishing properties to its destructive ones like the 1660 flooding of Münster by the Prince Bishop.
For his commission, Dennis will map the neighborhood of Berg Fidel, in southern Münster, “onto the cosmos and vice versa, constructing an observatory as a hyper-local calendric device,” according to a release. Ohtsubo, who has studied ikebana since the 1960s, will use local apple trees that have been cut down once they are no longer able to bear fruit and transform them into a large-scale installation in the center of Münster.
“An artwork in the public space need not compete for visibility in an already overly saturated world; it can offer time to witness, to feel, and to stay with what cannot readily be resolved,” WHW continued in its statement. “At a moment when political and economic propositions struggle to make a positive future imaginable, the faint hope of Skulptur Projekte 2027 is that such encounters with art in public space might allow for perspectives to be felt and acknowledged that are often misrepresented or obscured, without forcing consensus where none exists.”
The full list of announced commissions follows below. An asterisk indicates a previously announced commission.

US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu
As news emerged on Wednesday that the Democratic Party had won a landslide victory, regaining control of the US Congress, Israeli politicians, journalists and experts warned of the results' grave implications for Israel's national security, pointing to the declining standing of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the US.
Former Israeli prime minister Yair Lapid, who was re-elected to parliament last week as part of the centre-right Together alliance, said the US election results had "eliminated" any possibility of forming a unity government with Netanyahu.
"Israel cannot afford for him to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid said on X on Wednesday morning.
Recent Israeli reports indicated that US President Donald Trump is applying pressure on Netanyahu and the Israeli opposition leaders to form a unity government that will exclude extremists in order to advance his Middle Eastern policies.
Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats alliance, also described Netanyahu as a threat to Israel's security in the wake of the US election results, which saw progressive Democrats, including Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed – the first Muslim elected to the US Senate – win races across the country.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Owono enduring ‘hardest days of my life’ after De Miguel death
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Owono enduring ‘hardest days of my life’ after De Miguel death
Tenerife striker De Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries from a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono.
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday.
The 30-year-old Spanish footballer died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in the collision with Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who had raced into midfield to clear an aerial ball.
“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra on Wednesday.
“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.
“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.”
Spanish police sources told the AFP news agency that an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision.
Andorra players observed a minute’s silence on Wednesday before a voluntary training session, which Owono, 25, did not attend.
Owono received support from the president of the African country’s federation, Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, in a letter of condolence following De Miguel’s death.
“I feel compelled to convey all our solidarity and support at this time to our player Jesus Lazaro Owono,” Micha wrote.
“We know that, as the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress.
“From the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation, we offer him all our human and professional backing, fully aware of the harshness of this event, which no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.”
Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz posted on Instagram in support of Owono, whom he said was “deeply affected” by what had happened.
“Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone,” wrote Spatz.
“In football, unfortunate incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.”
Postponements
Earlier on Wednesday, it was confirmed that Tenerife and Andorra’s Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend would be postponed.
Tenerife were due to face Granada away from home, while Andorra were set to welcome Mallorca.
“After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game … this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes [stadium], has been postponed,” said Granada in a statement.
Mallorca said, “At times like this, respect and sensitivity in the face of a situation of profound grief must come first.”
The Spanish football federation postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches this week as a mark of respect following De Miguel’s death.
Tenerife plan to hold a tribute to De Miguel at the club’s stadium on Saturday, which supporters can attend, and are holding a six-day mourning period.
The club said the first team, board and staff will attend De Miguel’s funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo on the Spanish mainland, where he has family roots.
A minute of silence was held before Champions League matches on Tuesday in honour of the striker, with the same planned for the rest of the week’s fixtures, organised by European football’s governing body UEFA.

This is an entry from: Live: ‘It will crush us’: Israeli leaders in panic mode over fallout from US elections
Brent crude oil falls under $100 a barrel after Trump's midterm defeats
4 November 2026 16:27 GMT
Benchmark international oil contract Brent crude dropped more than four percent to under $100 per barrel on Wednesday following heavy defeats suffered by US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections.
The price of Brent crude for delivery in January went down 4.7 percent to $98.76 per barrel, hitting below $100 per barrel for the first time since early October.

https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/10/30/b.title: Brooklyn Crash Victim’s EMT Twin Sister Calls Out City, DSNY for Reckless Driving
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/10/30/b.author: Sam Brule
https://nyc.streetsblog.org/2026/10/30/b.text:
The victim, Siobhan Lynch, right, with her identical twin, Shannon on their 30th birthday — their last together.
A woman whose sister was killed earlier this week by a Department of Sanitation truck driver holds the driver and city responsible for the fatal crash — and plans to sue them over the tragedy, which she called “not an accident.”
“As someone who responds to emergencies on the daily, it was not an accident. The autopsy report says it was from blunt force trauma. Clearly, that’s 1,000s of pounds of pressure that hit her. So how fast were you turning?” Shannon Lynch said in an interview on Thursday, the day after the driver of a DSNY dump truck struck and killed her 30-year-old twin sister Siobhan at the corner of Cropsey Avenue and Bay Parkway in Brooklyn.
“These sanitation workers are getting away with too much. I want this man in jail. I want him arrested,” she said. “You killed my sister. You took the only person that I have away from me.”
Shannon, who works as an emergency medical technician, said Siobhan was hyper-vigilant about crossing the street because of her sister’s line of work. She told Streetsblog she sees Sanitation Department drivers speed and run red lights “all the time.”
“They do run a lot of red lights. I see it all the time. I don’t know why they do that. They are not an emergency vehicle. You are picking up trash,” Lynch said.
Siobhan was crossing Bay Parkway from Bensonhurst Park to the southeast corner of Bay Parkway and Cropsey Avenue when the DSNY driver turned right from Cropsey Avenue onto Bay Parkway and crushed her, causing severe body trauma.
Lynch described Siobhan as a beloved aunt who helped care for her sister’s kids, often accompanying them at the very intersection where she was killed.
“My sister always went over there because her boyfriend lived there, and she would take my kids to the park across the street there all the time,” the grieving sibling said.
“She was always careful crossing the street, like she — I made sure she was careful crossing the street because she was with my children, you know. And even on her own, you know, she would cross. She would make sure. She would wait. She wouldn’t jaywalk. She wouldn’t. She was like, ‘No, no, no,’ you know. So I, I don’t, I don’t know how this could happen,” Lynch said.
A source who reviewed the video said both the driver and pedestrian had the light. DSNY declined to comment on the details of the incident.
“This is a terrible tragedy, and our thoughts are with the family of the victim. DSNY is assisting NYPD with their ongoing investigation,” Deputy Commissioner Joshua Goodman said in a statement.
The intersection of Cropsey Avenue and Bay Parkway is one of the worst in the city, sluicing impatient drivers on both of the wide, two-way roadways onto or from the Belt Parkway, itself one of the most dangerous highways in the city.
In 2025, there were 30 reported crashes at just that intersection, injuring 21 people, including five pedestrians. Since 2021, there have been at least 106 reported crashes, injuring 77 people, including three cyclists and 18 pedestrians, according to city stats. (There are likely many more victims, but city crash data has not been updated since early June, for reasons that have never been explained by the Mamdani administration.)
In a 2025 presentation in support of a recently installed bus lane on Cropsey, the city Department of Transportation pointed out that the entire stretch of Bay Parkway, including Cropsey Avenue, is a “Vision Zero Priority Corridor” because 25 people were killed or seriously injured between 2019 and 2023.
Friends of Shannon Lynch started a GoFundMeto help her cover childcare costs.
Sam Brule is a senior at The New School. He’s previously worked at the New School Free Press, the Sopris Sun in Colorado, and most recently amNY. When he’s not writing, he works as a bike messenger.
