https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Novo projeto da prefeitura de Viamão ameaça devedores do IPTU e de outros tributos municipais
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Eugênio Bortolon
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Ativistas e organizações da sociedade civil de Viamão estão em pé de guerra com o prefeito Rafael Bortoletti Dalla Nora (PSDB), que mandou para a Câmara Municipal o Projeto de Lei 138/2026, que propõe a cessão onerosa de direitos creditórios do município. O que isso significa? É uma autorização ao município a realizar a venda ou transferência (cessão onerosa) de direitos creditórios, atingindo fundamentalmente os devedores de IPTU (Imposto Predial e Territorial Urbano) e outros tributos municipais. Ou repassar para terceiros o direito de receber dívidas ou créditos futuros que pertencem ao município em troca de recursos imediatos.
A proposta enviada por Bortoletti foi feita em regime de urgência – isto é, nenhum outro projeto corriqueiro que tramita na Câmara pode andar sem a aprovação imediata desta iniciativa.
Como as leis municipais ordinárias sancionadas em Viamão já estão na numeração da casa dos 5.600, o número 138 identifica especificamente o andamento desse projeto de autoria do Poder Executivo na Câmara de Vereadores. Naturalmente, a proposta vem provocando questionamentos e debates acirrados entre parlamentares da oposição no Legislativo. Eles vêm cobrando explicações detalhadas e maior transparência do governo em relação aos valores envolvidos, aos critérios técnicos adotados e aos reais impactos financeiros de longo prazo para a administração de Viamão.
A tramitação do projeto tomou conta dos debates da Câmara e de setores da sociedade. Na sessão ordinária de número 69, o projeto 138/2026 estava no centro das discussões, sob forte acompanhamento do plenário. Parlamentares da oposição reforçaram pedidos de esclarecimentos claros detalhando o volume real de créditos que serão vendidos e o percentual de deságio aplicado na transação com os bancos.
A pauta deve retornar para deliberação ou votação ainda no mês de novembro, segundo informações da assessoria de imprensa do Legislativo, à medida que os pareceres das comissões permanentes forem emitidos. As sessões plenárias ocorrem regularmente às terças e quintas-feiras, às 16h, e estão abertas à participação da comunidade no Plenário Tapir Rocha, além de serem transmitidas ao vivo pelo site da Câmara.
O projeto do prefeito é baseado na Lei Complementar 208, de origem do Senado Federal, sancionada pela presidência em julho de 2024, que alterou a lei dos direitos financeiros e o Código Tributário Nacional. O projeto municipal prevê a antecipação de receita, podendo, inclusive, ser dispensada de licitação para a transferência dos direitos sobre o crédito. As preocupações que levaram a que a sociedade de Viamão se motivasse são de duas ordens e estão relacionadas, por um lado e no curto a médio prazo, aos direitos humanos fundamentais das famílias à moradia e, por outro no médio e longo prazo, na capacidade de investimento futuro da administração pública municipal em políticas sociais e mesmo de infraestrutura.
Advogado tributarista
Conforme o advogado tributarista de Viamão, Heron de Moraes, o projeto cria condições para que pessoas que enfrentam dificuldades financeiras venham a perder seus bens, incluindo o imóvel único familiar. A razão é que a dívida de IPTU é a única que autoriza o imóvel em que a família reside. Ainda, a partir de sua futura (ou não) aprovação, o município passa a ter autorização para protestar com maior agilidade às dívidas existentes, com a consequência de que, assim que tiver sua dívida protestada, o nome do contribuinte é inserido automaticamente no Serasa e ficar com “nome sujo na praça”.
Heron diz que não pertence ao grupo político de resistência ao projeto, porém, como apoiador, contribui com uma análise jurídica sobre a iniciativa, em especial aos moradores que possuem débitos de IPTU inscritos ou não em Dívida Ativa. “A aprovação traz reflexos diretos, tais como: Intensificação do Protesto Extrajudicial e Interrupção da Prescrição. A fim de conferir liquidez e atratividade aos lotes de Dívida Ativa de IPTU ofertados no mercado, a Fazenda Municipal passará a protestar massivamente as Certidões de Dívida Ativa (CDAs) em Cartórios de Protesto de Títulos. Isso acarreta a negativação imediata do contribuinte nos órgãos de proteção ao crédito e a reinicialização da contagem do prazo prescricional quinquenal”, afirma.
“Com isso, a Administração Tributária passa a ter competência para requisitar informações cadastrais e patrimoniais do sujeito passivo a órgãos e entidades públicas ou privadas (bancos, registros de imóveis, Detran, CVM – Comissão de Valores Mobiliários”, reforça o advogado.
“Como reflexo no IPTU, Heron cita que o fisco local utilizará esse cruzamento de dados para identificar outros bens e ativos financeiros do devedor, acelerando pedidos de penhora do próprio imóvel gerador do imposto ou de constrições via SisbaJud (Sistema de Busca de Ativos do Poder Judiciário) em Execuções Fiscais”, garante.
O apelo por diálogo
Iliete Aparecida Citadin, educadora socioambiental e militante de movimento social, está também envolvida nas discussões do projeto e defende a retirada imediata do regime de urgência do projeto. “Precisamos de diálogo urgente”, apela. “Sem isso, o projeto é como uma navalha pronta para nos ferir”, enfatiza. “Queremos que a PL 138 tenha um debate amplo, inclusive com audiências públicas descentralizadas. Assim envolve e garante a participação das comunidades. Trazer um assunto tão sério como este, passando sem debate, sem nada, demonstra a impopularidade da vontade do executivo de Viamão”.
O pior, para ela, é que o projeto subiu para a Câmara num período importante para o país, as eleições do segundo turno. “Portanto, não foi noticiado, ficamos sabendo quase por um acaso, porque a mãe de uma participante do movimento ouviu um vereador falando numa rede social. Imediatamente chamou a atenção dela, pois percebeu a gravidade deste tipo de lei”, esclarece a educadora. Citadin ainda acrescenta que o projeto poderá ser votado nesta quinta-feira (5).
“Se continuar com a ameaça de maioria na Câmara e tocarem o projeto adiante, vamos ver o que fazer no que nos cabe na forma jurídica. Mas na questão de informar a população, não mediremos esforços para que as pessoas saibam que elas não têm um prefeito, tem um inimigo”, acusa.
E reforça: “Oferecer uma cidade cuidada, bonita, com manutenção permanente, atrai a população para o pagamento”. Para ela, os governos deveriam se preocupar em trabalhar na sociedade como funciona o investimento do tributo, mas ao contrário de trabalhar a cidadania, em época eleitoral, a cidadania vira favorável em troca do voto”.
A prefeitura não respondeu aos pedidos de entrevista. O espaço continua aberto.
Líder em inadimplência
Viamão ocupa, atualmente, pelo terceiro ano consecutivo, o 1° lugar no ranking de inadimplência de IPTU na região metropolitana. Tem cerca de 80 mil imóveis cadastrados. Entre os devedores, logo a seguir vem Alvorada. A iniciativa pode atingir mais de 50% da população do município. “Num contexto de alto endividamento das famílias brasileiras, este tende a ser um fator de intenso risco para os setores de baixa renda, com até um salário mínimo, que são imensa maioria no município”, afirma Iliete.
Por fim, dado que a cobrança de juros e multas fica restrita à mesma lógica atual do serviço público e que toda relação permanece sendo entre poder municipal e contribuinte, o atrativo para as empresas privadas – bancos e fundos de investimentos – se dará pelo deságio previsto na lei. Isto significa que a lógica será de que o município receba antecipadamente um valor menor do que as receitas futuras previstas.
A lei é originária de Brasília
A Lei Complementar 208 de 2024 é de origem do Poder Legislativo Federal. A legislação trouxe mudanças estruturais importantes no Direito Financeiro e no Direito Tributário brasileiro ao alterar a Lei nº 4.320/1964 e o Código Tributário Nacional (CTN).
Principais Pilares da LC 208/2024: Autoriza expressamente a União, os Estados, o Distrito Federal e os Municípios a ceder onerosamente direitos creditórios originados de créditos tributários e não tributários (como a dívida ativa) para pessoas jurídicas de direito privado ou fundos de investimento regulados pela CVM. A natureza, as garantias e as prerrogativas de cobrança original do crédito público ficam totalmente preservadas. Pelo menos 50% das receitas obtidas com essa cessão devem ser destinadas a regimes de previdência social e o restante a investimentos públicos.
Protesto Extrajudicial: Altera o artigo 174 do CTN para estabelecer que o protesto extrajudicial da Certidão de Dívida Ativa (CDA) passa a ser uma causa de interrupção do prazo prescricional de 5 anos. Com o protesto, a contagem do prazo para a execução judicial é zerada.
Acesso a Dados Cadastrais e Patrimoniais: Autoriza a administração tributária a requisitar informações cadastrais e patrimoniais de contribuintes junto a entidades e órgãos públicos ou privados. O compartilhamento de dados ocorre de forma direta para fins de fiscalização e cobrança, devendo respeitar a LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais).
O que diz a Confederação Nacional dos Municípios
Em nota, a Confederação Nacional dos Municípios (CNM) publicou nota em que entende que a securitização de créditos públicos pode ser uma ferramenta poderosa para melhorar a liquidez dos municípios. “Neste cenário de elevada complexidade e impacto financeiro das novas disposições legais, reconhece também os desafios associados à sua implementação e recomenda cautela para navegar com segurança e clareza no novo panorama legal estabelecido pela Lei Complementar 208, de 2 de julho de 2024, que, após 42 anos, alterou a redação da Lei 4.320/1964. Nesse sentido, a CNM publicou no seu site (www.cnm.org.br) Nota Técnica dando orientações pertinentes em observância para melhor aplicar a securitização.
Quem é o prefeito
Rafael Bortoletti Dalla Nora (PSDB) foi eleito prefeito de Viamão em 2024 com 49.914 votos, ou 48,49% dos votos válidos (dados a todos os candidatos). É um prefeito polêmico não só por esta questão, mas por outras também. Esteve envolvido em conduta proibida durante as eleições, relacionada à participação dele e do seu vice Marciel Fauri Bergmann em evento que marcou a abertura do Centro de Eventos do Parque SaintHilaire. Foi cassado.
Depois de idas e vindas, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) restabeleceu os mandatos, ao reformar decisão anterior que havia determinado a cassação dos diplomas e a realização de novas eleições no município. A decisão foi proferida pela ministra Estela Aranha, que também determinou a suspensão imediata das eleições suplementares previstas para abril de 2025.
Outra polêmica em que se envolveu durante o mandato foi a divulgação de conteúdo íntimo sem consentimento da vítima e por delito previsto no artigo 343 do Código Penal, referente à promessa de vantagens a testemunhas. No julgamento da apelação criminal interposta pela defesa, o Colegiado decidiu por redimensionar a pena imposta ao acusado, reduzindo-a para 6 anos, 4 meses e 18 dias de reclusão, a ser cumprida inicialmente em regime semiaberto, além de 15 dias-multa, à razão de um salário mínimo. Também ficou mantido o pagamento de indenização mínima à vítima no valor de R$ 50 mil.
Segundo a denúncia, o réu divulgou áudios íntimos de mulher, com quem manteve relacionamento amoroso, durante uma confraternização realizada em março de 2019, e posteriormente prometeu vantagem a testemunhas para que negassem os fatos perante a autoridade policial. A relatora do julgamento, desembargadora Vanessa Gastal de Magalhães, se manifestou com o entendimento de que a conduta do homem corresponde ao tipo penal descrito no art. 218-C do Código Penal e, portanto, deveriam ser afastadas as alegações de atipicidade da conduta.
Em seu voto, a magistrada destacou que áudios com descrição minuciosa de atos sexuais se enquadram na expressão “outro registro audiovisual” prevista na legislação, por representarem forma de violação à intimidade e à dignidade sexual da vítima. “A interpretação do tipo penal deve ser teleológica, buscando a proteção da dignidade e da intimidade sexual, bem jurídico tutelado pela norma. Os áudios divulgados, conforme se depreende do seu conteúdo e do relato das testemunhas, não eram meras conversas íntimas, mas verdadeiras áudio descrições de cenas sexuais, com riqueza de detalhes e simulação de atos”, salientou a relatora.

https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.title: Bassvictim: Peace + War review – like a thrillingly chaotic house party that goes on too long
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.author: Alexis Petridis
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.text:
Even by the standards of an age in which artists are encouraged to maintain a constant stream of new releases to ensure that they maintain a continual presence in an attention-deficit economy, there’s something pretty startling about Bassvictim’s work rate. Peace + War is the London-based duo’s fourth project in two years: 19 more tracks to add to the 31 they’ve already released since last January.
It’s a lot, but then, reading Bassvictim’s interviews you wonder if they’re simply splurging out material in the knowledge that their time is limited. The duo – Polish singer Maria Manow and Brooklyn-born producer Ike Clateman – really don’t give the impression of a band built for longevity. They have already announced their split on at least two separate occasions and lurid stories of a reportedly turbulent relationship.
At the end of 2025, they gave a tumultuous interview to Pitchfork that began with Manow taking ketamine to calm her down and got progressively more chaotic from there. She kept bursting into tears, threatened to quit yet again and suggested artists who were struggling for ideas “should take ketamine … and if some people die as a result of that, so be it”. (If you incline to the Daily Mail line that gen Z should consider bucking up their ideas a bit, you might note that at least some of her distress was apparently occasioned by losing her lucky hair slide, and that, at one point in the feature, it looks as if the evening’s gig might be derailed because she’d mislaid her vape.)
You hesitate to mention the 00s revivalist tag “indie sleaze”, because the thought of being labelled as such was one of the things that started Manow weeping, but you can see why the label has attached itself to them. The ongoing obsession of teens and twentysomethings with dissolute early 00s alt-rock and electro could be a screw-you reaction to growing up in a climate of constant nitpicking surveillance on social media, pressure to maintain a perfect Instagram-ready outward appearance, and lectures about health and abstinence from wellness influencers. If that’s the case, then Bassvictim, in all their confused, gobby combustibility, might well be its poster children. On Peace + War, Manow’s vocals frequently tend to yelling in the manner of someone in the throes of an implacable end-of-a-long-night meltdown: better that, the suggestion seems to be, than the scenario sketched out in the lyrics of I Don’t Know: “To me your life seems mid … plain girl, plain meals”.
More prosaically, echoes of several micro-genres from the era of Myspace and MP3 blogs gust through their sound. Electroclash is the obvious comparison, but as Peace + War progresses, you also catch distinct hints of witch house in the keening, echoing, atonal synths of Charred Glass, chiptune on Summer Song’s tinny vintage video game soundtrack aesthetic, and the decade’s wholehearted embrace of the kind of indie pop once reviled as irredeemably twee. Manow’s vocals keep slipping from the aforementioned yell into a slurred, childlike and occasionally melodically wayward tone; I Don’t Know’s lyrical bitterness is set to a melody so perkily simplistic it sounds like a nursery rhyme. Elsewhere, their penchant for multi-tracking vocals into faintly chaotic-sounding playground chants has a hint of the Go! Team about it, while a four-to-the-floor powered collaboration with underground rapper Fimiguerrero, inescapably – and not unpleasurably – evokes the period where UK rap briefly turned its attentions to chart-friendly house-fuelled commerciality.
They’re capable of writing nagging pop hooks, and of slipping into a more contemplative space – the beatless electronics of closer The End might glitch, yet there’s a lulling, becalmed quality about them nonetheless – but Peace + War is at its most exciting when the rough demo-like quality of its sound evokes a sense of teeming chaos. When layer after layer of vocals, spoken word and random interjections give you the impression it was recorded in the middle of a particularly messy house party; when huge basslines suddenly appear at a volume that means they drown out everything else; when its songs don’t so much come to a conclusion as collapse in front of you.
The problem is one of abundance. Even if you understand Bassvictim’s desire to splurge out material while they’ve still got the opportunity, this is music that works best in short bursts, and ideas run thin over the course of an hour. “There’s no more words left to say,” sings Manow towards the album’s conclusion, or at least she does eventually. It takes her a few goes to get the lyric right; the mistakes, punctuated by frustrated sighs, are left in. She sounds exhausted by the whole enterprise, and the listener may feel the same way some time before she does.

Piss – How Can You Act Opposite to This Emotion
  
Like a lot of 2026’s best albums, the cocktail of raw-throated punk noise, spoken word and sound collage on the Canadian quartet’s You Made Me/Skin on Linen is a challenging listen. But if you’re in the market for scourging fury, 2026 has produced nothing to compare.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5.title: ‘Healthcare not bombs’: How Gaza shaped Adam Hamawy’s path to US Congress
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5.text:
‘Healthcare not bombs’: How Gaza shaped Adam Hamawy’s path to US Congress
A former army surgeon and Gaza volunteer, Hamawy is the first Muslim American to be elected to the US Congress from New Jersey.
Adam Hamawy has seen death, devastation and the effects of hate on others for decades – as a first responder after the September 11 attacks, while serving in Iraq as a United States military surgeon, and more recently, on trips to Gaza while it has suffered under Israel’s genocide.
On Tuesday, he stood in front of supporters in Plainsboro, New Jersey, celebrating “hope” that he said he had gleaned from some of those victims of violence.
“To the men, women and children of Gaza and Palestine: Your smiles give me the hope and the courage to fight for a better world,” said the Egyptian-American surgeon, set to become New Jersey’s first Muslim US congressman.
It was the culmination of a winding path into politics for 56-year-old Hamawy, a US Army veteran and reconstructive surgeon who was one of eight Muslim Americans to win election races on Tuesday night, as Democrats took commanding control of both chambers of the US Congress.
Hamawy entered politics after participating in medical missions to Gaza in 2024 and 2025, experiences he said made it impossible for him to return to normal life.
He campaigned for New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District on a platform of “healthcare not bombs”, pledging to challenge a system that “funds genocide [in Gaza] while trapping us all here in medical debt”.
But Hamawy’s bid for the House of Representatives was met with a wave of attacks that he described as “anti-Muslim”, as well as scrutiny over his past association with a sheikh later convicted of seditious conspiracy.
“I have never seen anti-Muslim hate as open and as loud and as accepted as it is today,” said Hamawy, who served for eight years as a US Army officer, including a deployment to Iraq as a combat surgeon.
“Let me say this to anyone who still believes that Muslims are strangers here. To every Muslim child who’s been told that you don’t belong: You belong,” he said.
The American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC) welcomed Hamawy’s victory, along with those of other “principled candidates”.
“Hamawy witnessed the horrors of Israel’s genocide in Gaza firsthand,” the ADC said. “Now, he will take his place in the very Congress that funded and enabled those atrocities, bringing the testimony of what he witnessed directly to the lawmakers responsible for sustaining US support for Israel’s genocide.”
‘The doctor who saved my life’
Hamawy was born in Egypt, and his family moved to New Jersey when he was a baby. Raised in Old Bridge, New Jersey, Hamawy completed his undergraduate studies at Rutgers University and earned a medical degree from New Jersey Medical School.
He later joined the New Jersey National Guard and worked as a combat trauma surgeon for the US Army, including on a nine-month deployment to Baghdad, Iraq in 2004.
It was there that Hamawy treated now-Illinois Senator Tammy Duckworth, who at the time was a US Army helicopter pilot. Duckworth was badly injured when her helicopter was shot down by Iraqi fighters in November 2004, and says Hamawy saved her life and one of her limbs.
“He is the doctor who not only saved my life, but was able to prevent me from becoming a triple amputee by employing a vascular procedure that he’d just learned in medical school,” said Duckworth, who lost both her legs.
The Illinois senator was the first serving US congressperson to endorse Hamawy back in January, calling him a leader with the courage to “speak truth to power” and “willingness to call out injustices at home and abroad”.
Hamawy retired from the army with the rank of lieutenant colonel in 2011. In the years leading up to and following his retirement, he put his medical skills to use in numerous humanitarian missions abroad, including treating victims of war and disaster in Haiti, Jordan, Lebanon and Gaza.
‘Complete destruction’ in Gaza
During Hamawy’s first mission to Gaza in 2024, he said the level of destruction was unlike anything he had ever seen before.
“This is not like a war. This is just like complete, utter destruction,” said Hamawy in an interview from the enclave, adding that he could only define what was happening there “as a genocide”.
“When the hospital shakes and I see the bodies come in, I’m paying for it with my tax dollars,” he later said in an interview with The Guardian. “I don’t want my tax dollars doing that.”
While he treated patients at Gaza’s European Hospital in 2024, Israel seized the Rafah border crossing, temporarily trapping Hamawy and his colleagues in the enclave. Hamawy refused to be evacuated until he was assured non-American members of his team would also be able to leave.
‘Bigoted’ attacks
Hamawy declared his congressional candidacy in January after the retirement announcement of Representative Bonnie Watson Coleman. He quickly faced fierce criticism from opponents, including Democratic challenger Adrian Mapp, who called him a “radical extremist”.
Mapp and other critics pointed to Hamawy’s past association with Omar Abdel Rahman, known as the “Blind Sheikh”, who was later convicted of several “terrorism” charges, including in connection with the 1993 World Trade Center bombing. Hamawy, in his early 20s, travelled to a conference with Abdel Rahman and others and later was called as a defence witness at Abdel Rahman’s trial.
Hawamy has condemned Abdel Rahman’s “violent rhetoric and actions” and says he testified at his trial out of a sense of “civic duty”.
Still, several New Jersey politicians accused Hamawy of failing to answer for his connection to Abdel Rahman, who died in 2017.
“As a Muslim, they’re always going to find something to attack,” Hamawy told local media earlier this year, as his campaign called the scrutiny “gross and bigoted”.
After winning his congressional race, Hamawy said the hate he had faced had also been “targeted against my family, my coworkers, my friends”, and that his “loyalty” and “patriotism” had been questioned.
Selaedin Maksut, executive director of the New Jersey chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations, said, “Islamophobic rhetoric employed by so many candidates miserably backfired this election season.”
“New Jersey is a better place because American Muslims are standing up, speaking out, and fighting for a more just future for all,” said Maksut.
‘Broken and rigged system’
Hamawy’s platform priorities included healthcare for all, ending medical and student debt, and abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which he has called an agency “full of neo-Nazis”.
He has said the push for universal healthcare is personal for him, as a physician “who sees firsthand how insurance companies and the rest of our absurd system fail patients and providers alike”.
On foreign policy, Hamawy opposes the war on Iran, which he has called “illegal and immoral”, and advocates an end to US military aid to Israel. He has pledged to fight for “for justice and equal rights for Palestinians, including support for the Palestinian right of return under international law”.
The surgeon-turned-congressman has described his policy goals as “interconnected”.
“They are solutions to a crisis that was born out of a broken and rigged political and economical system,” he said after winning a hard-fought Democratic primary race in June.
“A system that floods money overseas to bomb children’s schools while at the same time [saying] that childcare here in America [is a] pie-in-the-sky idea.”

https://www.humanite.fr/-/-/a-bordeaux-6.title: A Bordeaux, 60 000 personnes manifestent dans le calme
https://www.humanite.fr/-/-/a-bordeaux-6.text:
Après plus d’un mois de mouvement lycéen et des manifestations qui ont réuni des centaines de milliers de personnes dans les rues notamment les trois derniers samedis, l’heure est plus que jamais à la convergence des luttes ce jeudi 5 novembre. Augmentation des salaires, défense des services publics, justice fiscale, refus du budget d’austérité à 54 milliards soumis au parlement par Sébastien Lecornu…
Autant de mots d’ordre de l’intersyndicale pour cette journée de grève et de manifestations auxquels s’ajoutent les revendications de la jeunesse pour le droit d’étudier dans de bonnes conditions (remplacement des profs, réhabilitation des locaux, suppression de Parcoursup…).
1 512 appels à la grève et plus de 260 manifestations à travers l’Hexagone étaient recensés par la CGT ce jeudi matin. « Cela va être une belle mobilisation », observe Marylise Léon, secrétaire générale de la CFDT, avançant des remontées du même ordre que ce « qu’on avait sur les retraites ».
« Cette journée de grève a une double utilité : obtenir les hausses de salaire et contrer un budget qui fait payer aux travailleurs, aux précaires et aux retraités la facture des politiques en faveur des ultra-riches et des grandes entreprises », résume Thomas Vacheron, secrétaire confédéral CGT.
Le gouvernement, lui, continue de jouer la carte de la répression avec des manifestations entravées par les préfectures comme à Paris où le parcours, finalement au départ de République, n’a été arrêté qu’à la dernière minute. De son côté, le ministre de l’Intérieur Laurent Nuñez a annoncé mobiliser 70 000 policiers et gendarmes, promettant « une réponse d’une extrême fermeté » aux éventuels « débordements ». Face à la réponse autoritaire du gouvernement qui tente ainsi d’esquiver une réponse sur le fond des revendications, de nombreuses organisations ont dénoncé hier les attaques contre l’État de droit.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: China: Brasil de Fato lança série documental sobre a Longa Marcha, 90 anos depois da vitória
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Mauro Ramos
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Brasil de Fato lança, neste mês, “Como a Longa Marcha forjou a Nova China”, em cinco capítulos gravados nas províncias de Jiangxi, Guizhou e Gansu, e na Região Autônoma de Ningxia. A série começa em Ruijin, onde foi instaurada a Base Central Soviética de 1931 a 1934, como centro da República Soviética da China, a primeira experiência de governo criada pelo Partido Comunista da China (PCCh).
A Longa Marcha do Exército Vermelho de Operários e Camponeses, braço armado do PCCh, durou dois anos, de outubro de 1934 a outubro de 1936, e passou pelo território de 14 províncias. Sob um cerco crescente do Kuomintang, Partido Nacionalista da China, o exército decidiu romper o bloqueio a Ruijin. O objetivo era reorganizar as forças no oeste da província de Hunan, mas os planos foram mudando em função das condições da guerra e as rotas precisaram ser refeitas várias vezes. A coluna mais longa percorreu mais de 12 mil quilômetros; somando as quatro forças principais do exército (a 1ª Frente, 4ª Frente e a 2ª Frente, formada pelo 2º e 6º Corpos, e o 25º Exército Vermelho), o percurso passou de 30 mil quilômetros. 
Em 1934, Sun Daofa saiu do vilarejo de Tantou, em Yudu, província de Jiangxi, para se somar ao Exército Vermelho. Ele foi uma das dezenas de milhares que morreram na primeira grande batalha da Longa Marcha, no rio Xiang. Seu filho, Sun Guanfa, é um dos 20 entrevistados da série, junto a pesquisadores do Instituto Central de História do Partido e do memorial da Conferência de Zunyi, trabalhadoras dos memoriais de Ruijin, Lazikou e Huining e atores e atrizes de “A Primeira Travessia da Longa Marcha”, a primeira superprodução do turismo vermelho chinês, em cartaz desde março de 2023 no Grande Teatro da Longa Marcha de Yudu.
Nas entrevistas, os entrevistados falam sobre o que é conhecido atualmente como Espírito da Longa Marcha, o legado dessa façanha para a construção do país, o que o Partido Comunista e o Exército Vermelho aprenderam sobre a China que atravessavam, e como a própria Longa Marcha foi uma parte essencial do processo de construção de ambos. Assim, a marcha foi desenvolvendo e implementando a abordagem sobre a diversidade étnica do país, e o pensamento militar e político de Mao Zedong.
Em novembro de 1931, o congresso de Ruijin aprovou a Lei Agrária, que confiscou sem indenização as terras dos latifundiários e as distribuiu aos camponeses, marcando a centralidade da questão agrária para a revolução chinesa. A redistribuição da terra ia sendo feita por onde a Longa Marcha passava, somando adeptos ao Partido e ao Exército Vermelho.
A 1ª Frente, 4ª Frente e parte da 2ª Frente se encontraram em Huining em 9 de outubro de 1936 e, em 22 de outubro, as lideranças e as principais forças da 1ª e 2ª frentes se encontraram em Jiangtaibao (hoje Ningxia), marcando o fim oficial da Longa Marcha.
A série estreia neste mês no canal do Brasil de Fato no YouTube.

https://taz.de/Hubert-Aiwanger-gestorben.title: Hubert Aiwanger gestorben: Er war so frei
https://taz.de/Hubert-Aiwanger-gestorben.author: Dominik Baur
https://taz.de/Hubert-Aiwanger-gestorben.text:
Hubert Aiwanger gestorben: Er war so frei
Hubert Aiwanger fischte als Chef der Freien Wähler unverhohlen am rechten Rand. Aber er machte seine Partei auch zu einer regierungsfähigen Kraft. Ein Nachruf.
„Streitbar“ – es ist das Adjektiv, auf das sich alle in ihren Reaktionen auf den Tod von Bayerns stellvertretendem Ministerpräsidenten Hubert Aiwanger nach dem ersten Schock einigen können. Vom baden-württembergischen Ministerpräsidenten Cem Özdemir (Grüne) bis zu seinem nordrhein-westfälischen Amtskollegen Hendrik Wüst (CDU), vom CSU-Fraktionschef im Bayerischen Landtag, Klaus Holetschek, bis zu dessen SPD-Amtskollegen Holger Grießhammer, sie alle belegen den Verstorbenen mit dieser Vokabel.
Fragt sich natürlich, was das heißen soll: streitbar. Ist das einer, der den Streit sucht? Einer, mit dem man gut streiten konnte? Über dessen Ansichten sich streiten ließe? Oder ist es nur eine Umschreibung für ein weniger freundliches Adjektiv – umstritten? Es ist nicht gewagt, zumindest zu vermuten, dass die Floskel der Politiker etwas Distanz zum Ausdruck bringen soll, ohne den nötigen Anstand angesichts der menschlichen Tragödie missen zu lassen.
Denn natürlich war es ein Schock, als die Nachricht am Mittwochabend bekannt wurde, dass der Politiker in einem Hotelzimmer in Berlin leblos aufgefunden worden war. Aiwanger war gerade erst 55 Jahre alt, über größere gesundheitliche Beschwerden war nichts bekannt. Mit seiner Partnerin, der Regensburger Landrätin Tanja Schweiger, hatte er zwei Söhne im Schulalter.
Enfant terrible der Staatsregierung
Aufgewachsen ist Aiwanger auf einem Bauernhof im Landkreis Landshut in Niederbayern, den er noch lange – auch noch während seiner aktiven Politikerlaufbahn – gemeinsam mit den Eltern bewirtschaftete. Er engagierte sich in der Katholischen Landjugendbewegung, sein politisches Weck-Erlebnis, wie er es nannte, war Tschernobyl. In die aktive Politik ging er erst mit 30, dann ging es aber umso rasanter: Zunächst übernahm er für die Freien Wähler kommunale Ämter, 2003 die Organisation des Landtagswahlkampfs, 2006 den Landesvorsitz. 2008 zogen die Freien Wähler schließlich mit ihm als Galionsfigur in den Landtag ein, 10 Jahre später auch in die Staatsregierung, in der er selbst den Posten des Wirtschaftsministers und des stellvertretenden Ministerpräsidenten übernahm. Und gerne auch den des Enfant terrible. Oder anders formuliert: des Streitbaren.
Unter den Überbegriff des Streitbaren muss dann wohl auch so etwas subsumiert werden wie die Flugblattaffäre, die mitten im bayerischen Landtagswahlkampf 2023 die politische Landschaft erschütterte. Dabei war es gar nicht so sehr das Flugblatt an sich, das Aiwanger als Schüler bei sich getragen hatte. Sosehr einen der menschenverachtende Antisemitismus des Pamphlets auch abstoßen musste, so konnte man es als eine Jugendsünde verbuchen, Aiwanger zugutehalten, dass er in seiner Zeit als erwachsener Politiker niemals mit irgendwelchen antisemitischen Äußerungen aufgefallen war. Doch den trotzigen Umgang mit der Affäre, den – letztlich sogar erfolgreichen – Versuch, damit im Wahlkampf Kapital zu schlagen, hat man ihm nicht nur beim Koalitionspartner CSU schwer verübelt.
Schon vor dieser Flugblattaffäre hatte Grünen-Fraktionschefin Katharina Schulze ihn als „astreinen Rechtspopulisten“ bezeichnet, und Innenminister Joachim Herrmann (CSU) verglich ihn mit Querdenkern, Reichsbürgern und Klimaklebern.
„Mei, der Hubsi“
Schon vor der Affäre hatte Aiwanger in diesem Wahlkampf damit begonnen, immer unverhohlener am rechten Rand zu fischen. Besonders in Erinnerung blieb er mit seinem Auftritt auf der von der – nun ja, mehr als streitbaren – ehemaligen Kabarettistin Monika Gruber organisierten Demonstration gegen das als Heizungsgesetz berühmt gewordene Gebäudeenergiegesetz der Ampel in Erding. Dort rief er der Menge zu, man müsse sich die Demokratie zurückholen. Eine bemerkenswerte Aussage für den zweithöchsten Repräsentanten der demokratisch gewählten bayerischen Staatsregierung.
Ein paar Monate nach der Wahl schließlich versuchte sich Aiwanger an die Spitze der Bauernproteste zu stellen – auch dies sehr zum Missfallen der CSU, die ihm „Demo-Hopping“ und die Vernachlässigung seines Hauptjobs als Wirtschaftsminister vorwarf.
Trotz allem konnte sich der Politiker dabei immer einer gewissen, ihm qua Amt eigentlich nicht zustehenden Narrenfreiheit bedienen. Wie? Er nahm sie sich einfach, die Freiheit. „Mei, der Hubsi“, hieß es dann. Und ein paar Tage später lief eine andere Sau durchs Dorf.
Die Probleme der kleinen Leute
Was allerdings jenseits des Streitbaren bleiben wird: sein leidenschaftlicher Einsatz für Wasserstoff und Windkraft, vielleicht auch der ebenso leidenschaftliche Kampf gegen den Wolf, vor allem aber das, was er für die Freien Wähler vollbracht hat. Die Partei, die bis dato eigentlich nicht viel mehr gewesen war als ein Konglomerat verschiedener Wählervereinigungen, hievte er quasi im Alleingang in die Landespolitik.
Dabei setzte er auf das, was die Freien Wähler schon in den Kommunen stark gemacht hatte: die Konzentration auf die Probleme der kleinen Leute vor Ort. Und bei Aiwanger hieß das immer zugleich auch: der kleinen Leute auf dem Lande. Seit 18 Jahren gehören die Freien Wähler nun zum festen Bestandteil der bayerischen Landespolitik. In den Umfragen lagen sie zuletzt stabil bei etwa 9 Prozent.
Auch der Umstand, dass Aiwanger maßgeblich dazu beitrug, das Ende der CSU-Alleinherrschaften in Bayern zu besiegeln, und vielleicht sogar der AfD die eine oder andere Stimme wegnahm: Das ist letztlich etwas, was ihm nicht nur politische Freunde zugutehalten.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. So viele unterstützen freiwillig und regelmäßig. Noch nicht dabei? Werden Sie jetzt Teil der Community! Jetzt unterstützen

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5.title: Could the US midterms further isolate Israel in Washington?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5.text:
Could the US midterms further isolate Israel in Washington?
The midterms showed that challenging support for Israel can win votes. But changing US foreign policy may be harder.
As the midterm votes trickled in on Tuesday and Democrats locked up majorities in both chambers of the United States Congress, Republicans began pointing fingers at the Trump administration’s increasingly unpopular foreign policies.
“The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone,” Vice President JD Vance said on X, blaming the war on Iran, which has triggered soaring fuel prices and a $47bn bill, for souring voters on the Republican Party. Many, already appalled at US-funded Israeli genocide in Gaza and the occupation of southern Lebanon, also view the Trump administration as having been convinced to launch strikes on Iran on February 28 by Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu government, which insisted without evidence that Iran was “close” to developing a nuclear weapon.
An unnamed pollster, Vance said, had asked voters who had switched parties for this election what would bring them back. Summing up the causes for their displeasure with Trump’s government, they said they wanted an end to the war on Iran, action on the cost of living, a return to “America First” and a fundamental change in Washington’s relationship with Israel.
All of it, voters say, went directly against Trump’s campaign promises to end the US involvement in foreign wars and to bring down the cost of living.
About six in 10 voters surveyed by The Associated Press said that going to war with Iran was the wrong decision. Even more called the cost of living key to their decision about how to vote in the midterm elections. “Voters may not have been thinking about the specific details of the conflict, but they connected the war with the rise of the cost of living in the United States, and punished Republicans for it,” Andrew Payne of the Chatham House think tank told Al Jazeera.
Meanwhile in Detroit, Michigan’s Democratic senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed had called for an end to US military assistance to Israel, a position that experts say echoed the “America First” message on which many Republicans had won previous midterm races. He won his contest despite a vigorous campaign by the Republicans, and funded by the deep-pocketed, pro-Israel AIPAC lobby group. Although El-Sayed’s campaign focused primarily on healthcare and the cost of living, it may have been anger towards Israel that propelled the first Muslim into the US Senate.
“We don’t want our money sent to do apartheid or genocide or war,” El-Sayed told supporters from the podium, where he also took a jab at Vance. The two politicians sit at opposite ends of the political spectrum, but Vance’s diagnosis signals, at the very least, a rift in the Republican alliance with Netanyahu.
Payne said he believes a broader Republican realignment remains unlikely at this stage. But with Democrats winning so handily and criticism of Israel front and centre in some of their biggest swing-state upsets, he said that “the party could be emboldened to take an even tougher line moving forward.”
“There are very few issues on which we’ll see such a stark partisan contrast, making it one of the most likely to cut through in the presidential campaign in 2028,” Payne said.
Where AIPAC lost ground
On Wednesday night, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), the major US pro-Israel lobby which raises funds in support of pro-Israel political candidates, claimed more than “234 candidates” supported by its members had won their seats.
The group’s post on X congratulated Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries, the two Democratic leaders, as a swift reminder that it maintains support from both parties.
But the picture looks worse for AIPAC when measured by where its money went. A Responsible Statecraft report has found that AIPAC’s super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other political committees spent $84.1m on races. Of that, $55.3m went on races where their preferred candidate lost. In 2022 and 2024, by comparison, 69 percent and 87 percent of UDP’s spending went to races where its preferred candidates won.
It was Abdul El-Sayed’s Michigan race that proved to be the Israeli lobby’s most expensive setback. Responsible Statecraft put UDP’s spending on efforts to defeat El-Sayed at $31.47m across the primary and general election campaign periods. El-Sayed won both, and for Democrats weighing whether to challenge the party’s position on Israel, his victory establishes a strong precedent in which a candidate called for an end to military aid to Israel, withstood heavy outside donor spending and still won a statewide race in a swing state that Trump won in 2024.
Trump himself had already signalled that he understood the political cost. On election day, he said Washington would end annual military aid to Israel after this year, taking away what he called a “bad talking point” for Democrats. The existing agreement provides for $3.8bn a year through September 2028. Trump offered few details about how he would bring an early end to the funding and said the US would keep selling Israel weapons, prompting scepticism from observers.
What, if anything, could change for Gaza now?
Once Democrats take control of both houses, they are likely to use committee hearings and investigations to probe what both the Biden and Trump administrations knew about how Israel was using US weapons in Gaza, and why weapon transfers continued amid allegations of grave violations of international law, experts told Al Jazeera. Lawmakers can also seek conditions for future military funding and force votes on individual sales.
The appetite for such votes has grown over time. In January 2024, 11 senators backed an effort by Senator Bernie Sanders to require the US Department of State to report on Israel’s human rights record. A motion to advance a measure blocking a weapons sale drew 27 in July 2025. In April this year, 40 senators voted to advance a measure opposing a sale of military bulldozers to Israel, and 36 backed a similar move on 1,000-pound bombs.
A Democratic majority could possibly tip the balance in favour of some sort of partial ban on weapons sales. But Daniel Levy, president of the US/ Middle East Project (USMEP) and a former Israeli peace negotiator, told Al Jazeera that would likely be upended by Trump’s use of the presidential veto. On Tuesday, Trump told Fox News he plans to use the veto to block “insane” Democratic policies in Congress. Overriding a veto requires a two-thirds majority in both houses of Congress, which the Democrats are unlikely to be able to secure.
“I would not underestimate the extent to which executive privilege can be deployed in the ways this administration has deployed it, approaching and crossing lines that the US system of checks and balances should have enforced, but hasn’t,” Levy said.
Congress can put US support for Israel under greater scrutiny, but analysts say unpicking the security ties that bind the two countries will be a lot trickier.
“We might start to see a tougher line, but there are deeper structural issues at play that transcend Congress,” said Simon Mabon, a professor of international politics at Lancaster University. “They are tied to US institutions and other parts of the government, including military collaboration.”
“Democrats might start to capitalise on waning public support for Israel, but there are limits to what they can do,” Mabon said.
Rebuilding support for Israel
Since the Republican defeat this week, AIPAC has told its members it is “determined to expand political activism in the cycles ahead”.
Levy said that “the Israel lobby can still spend enough to keep lawmakers on board, and if ties in technology, AI, military AI and the wider economy hold, Israel may be able to ride out much of the pressure for change.”
He added that much of the lobby may also present dwindling support for Israel as a problem with Netanyahu or with far-right figures such as Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, rather than the Israeli state’s almost cross-party support for the war with Iran and strikes on Gaza.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Yair Lapid attempted a version of that argument on X on Wednesday. “These people aren’t against Israel. They’re against extremist ministers who say crazy things. They’re against settler violence; they’re against a government they don’t understand; they’re mainly against Netanyahu – for them, anything connected to him is toxic.”
He also faulted Netanyahu for openly siding with Republicans and urged the next Israeli government to meet both parties in Congress and hear their criticisms. He hopes a new, more liberal, government in Israel could reopen the closing doors with Washington’s lawmakers.
But the harder task would be persuading voters who object to US support for the genocide in Gaza and the Iran war, that changing Israel’s leadership would change those policies.
“Many voters believe the [Iran] war took place at Israel’s behest and would not have happened without Israel dragging the United States into it,” Levy said.
Analysts say it is unclear whether this will translate into policies that materially change the course of Israel’s genocidal policy in Gaza. What is clear is that this has been a bad election for Israel, as criticism of the country gains ground and moves into mainstream US political debate.
“For many voters, particularly Democrats, it also comes after several years of what they see as US complicity in the horrors of Israel’s war on Gaza,” Levy added.

5 novembre : « Plus de 250 000 manifestants » dans 73 villes à 13 heures, coup d'envoi de la manifestation parisienne au départ de République… Suivez en direct la mobilisation
L'essentiel
- Ce jeudi à 13 heures, la CGT a recensé « plus de 250 000 manifestants » dans 73 villes. « Le message est « rien ne nous arrêtera, la seule chose qui fera cesser la mobilisation est la réponse aux revendications » », a déclaré la secrétaire générale de la CGT, Sophie Binet.
- Fidèle à sa stratégie répressive, le ministre de l’Intérieur Laurent Nuñez a annoncé mercredi soir mobiliser 70 000 policiers et gendarmes, promettant « une réponse d’une extrême fermeté » aux éventuels « débordements ».
Le Direct
15h32
A Bordeaux, 60 000 personnes manifestent dans le calme
15h00 Pour approfondir
Les propositions du PCF pour la jeunesse et le pouvoir d'achat
Alors que les lycées se mobilisent toujours et que les travailleurs rejoignent la grève ce 5 novembre pour dénoncer la vie chère et la dégradation des services publics, l’Humanité reçoit Léna Raud, porte-parole du Parti communiste français (PCF), pour discuter des enjeux du mouvement social actuel tels que la construction du rapport de force, la répression policière et judiciaire des jeunes manifestants, ainsi que le plan d’urgence de 10 milliards d’euros porté par le PCF pour l’école et la jeunesse.
À suivre ici :
14h50
À Toulouse, les CRS empêchent le cortège d'avancer
Les CRS empêchent le cortège toulousain d’avancer sur le tracé classique dès le début de la manifestation. Ils exigent que la manifestation aille dans le sens opposé.
14h48
A Rennes, les CRS viennent de charger la tête de cortège
A Rennes, les CRS ont opéré une première charge, en pleine manifestation, contre la tête de manifestation, relève Audrey Loussouarn. Notre correspondante indique que quelques individus, ont “lancé des cailloux” sur les CRS. La ligne de CRS aurait remonté en courant vers le cortège, tandis que des camions les ont suivis.
C’est la tête de cortège, avec “ses drapeaux politiques et syndicaux”, qui ont été touchés. Audrey Loussouarn relève que des manifestants scandent “Calmez vous calmez vous”, aux CRS, tandis que sur une pancarte de début de cortège est inscrit: “Tape pas plus fort, je ne comprends toujours pas”.
Selon notre correspondante sur place, “il commence à y avoir du fumigène et ça crie ACAB! en boucle”, soit une tension qui devient palpable.
14h45
À Paris, les manifestants font une minute de silence en hommage à Pengo Bossio Wangi
Un peu après 14 heures, en plein milieu du boulevard Voltaire à Paris, les manifestants ont laissé place au silence pour rendre hommage à Pengo Bossio Wangi. L’homme de 26 ans a été victime d’un attentat raciste dans les Yvelines le 23 octobre. L’intersyndicale a ensuite dénoncé « les discours politiques » qui ont conduit à cet acte.
14h30
55 000 manifestants à Lyon selon l'intersyndicale
Après plus de deux heures de manifestation, le cortège lyonnais a rejoint son point de chute, place Jean Macé. L’intersyndicale dénombre 55 000 manifestants contre 30 500 selon la préfecture du Rhône.

Yemen: Saudi air strikes reported in Sanaa, clashes in Lahij governorate
Houthi affiliated media is reporting air strikes targeting the Hamdan district in Sanaa.
Military spokesman Yahya Saree said 12 people, including six children, were killed in Saudi strikes in Yemen on Wednesday, most in Taiz province.
Saudi Arabia carried out 104 air strikes and missile attacks in Sanaa, Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, Amran, Marib, Taiz and Lahij, the Ansar Allah spokesperson said.
Meanwhile, Al Jazeera reports clashes between government forces and the Houthis on the al-Maqatra front, in the Lahij governorate.
According to the report, government forces claim to have “neutralised” military vehicles and personnel in the skirmishes.
Al Jazeera also reports an escalating humanitarian crisis in Taiz, where civilians are dying as a result of shelling and the ongoing siege.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Palhaço Gambiarra celebra 10 anos de carreira com apresentações gratuitas no Agreste e Sertão de Pernambuco
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Fátima Pereira
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Palhaço Gambiarra dá continuidade à circulação estadual do espetáculo autoral “10 Anos Não São 10 Dias” com apresentações gratuitas em Arcoverde, na sexta (6), às 18 horas, no Centro Cultural Riso da Terra; em Buíque, nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro, às 17 horas, no Terreiro Dona Beiga e na comunidade do Pico, respectivamente; e em São José do Belmonte, no Sertão Central, com data e local ainda a serem definidos.
A iniciativa celebra os dez anos de trajetória do artista pernambucano na palhaçaria popular e promove encontros entre diferentes gerações de artistas, comunidades e expressões da cultura popular.
Natural de Camaragibe, na Região Metropolitana do Recife (RMR), Dú Yândi Ramos dos Santos, conhecido artisticamente como Palhaço Gambiarra, constrói a circulação a partir da relação entre circo, arte de rua e poesia. A programação é gratuita, tem classificação indicativa livre e conta com recurso de acessibilidade comunicacional em Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras).
Em cada município, o artista reúne profissionais locais e convidados para compartilhar experiências, valorizar saberes tradicionais e fortalecer vínculos entre os territórios. O projeto também promove rodas de diálogo, aproximando o público da trajetória dos artistas e das diferentes formas de transmissão da cultura circense.
“Mais do que uma rota de apresentações, a circulação é pensada a partir das relações feitas por diferentes territórios e da continuidade da trajetória artístico-cultural. O percurso conecta a Região Metropolitana do Recife ao Agreste e ao Sertão, transformando a estrada em espaço de encontro, troca de saberes e reconhecimento das diversas expressões que compõem a cultura pernambucana”, destaca Gambiarra.
A primeira parada da programação no interior será em Arcoverde, no Sertão do Moxotó. Na sexta-feira (6), às 18h, o Centro Cultural Riso da Terra, localizado no bairro São Miguel, recebe uma edição do Palco Aberto acompanhada de roda de diálogo. A atividade será conduzida pelo Palhaço Gambiarra, que divide o encontro com os artistas Amaik, Palhaço Salsicha e Palhaço Pinóquio.
Amaik é natural do Cabo de Santo Agostinho e reside em Arcoverde. Salsicha nasceu em Sumé, no Cariri paraibano, enquanto Pinóquio é de São Lourenço da Mata, em Pernambuco.
No Agreste, a programação chega à zona rural de Buíque, município vizinho a Arcoverde. No sábado (7), às 17h, o Terreiro Dona Beiga recebe o Palco Aberto. Já no domingo (8), também às 17h, a atividade acontece na comunidade do Pico, com apresentação e roda de diálogo. Os encontros são realizados em parceria com o Sítio Alcobaça.
Além dos artistas que integram a programação, os encontros em Buíque contam com a participação dos palhaços Sequinho, Salsicha e Pinóquio. A circulação também prevê a presença de outros artistas, palhaças, palhaços e profissionais da educação e da arte.
A escolha dos territórios está relacionada à trajetória de Gambiarra e às parcerias construídas ao longo dos anos. Em Buíque, o Sítio Alcobaça já recebeu ações de palhaçaria popular e atividades como o São João Rural e o Dia das Crianças. Em Arcoverde, o artista destaca a importância das primeiras apresentações de sua carreira solo e da relação com o Centro Cultural Riso da Terra.
“Buíque, por exemplo, é um território agrestino onde existe uma relação afetiva e artística desenvolvida historicamente. Entre as memórias estão as parcerias com o Sítio Alcobaça, espaço que recebeu diversas ações de palhaçaria popular e atividades como São João Rural e Dia das Crianças. O município representa a possibilidade de reencontrar públicos, vínculos e paisagens que compõem essa caminhada. No Sertão, Arcoverde é uma das primeiras cidades que recebeu apresentações de carreira solo. Reforço sobre a parceria com o Centro Cultural Riso da Terra, que fortalece o elo com artistas e iniciativas culturais territoriais. Já São José do Belmonte, cidade com uma dimensão de memória, cultura popular e identidade sertaneja, amplia a circulação para um território de tradições, narrativas e expressões artísticas”, conta.
A passagem por São José do Belmonte amplia o alcance da iniciativa para o Sertão Central. A cidade, reconhecida pela relação com a memória e as tradições sertanejas, integra o percurso que conecta diferentes regiões do estado.
A circulação estadual começou em setembro, em Camaragibe, cidade onde Gambiarra iniciou sua trajetória artística. A primeira edição aconteceu na Praça de Camaragibe, no bairro Vila da Inabi, com o artista como mestre de cerimônia e a participação de profissionais ligados à palhaçaria e ao circo.
Na ocasião, o público acompanhou números de malabarismo, esquetes de palhaçaria e performances de pirofagia. Participaram o Palhaço Xuvisco, o mestre Pinóquio, a artista Ynsany Dama Vermelha e os Irmãos Gandaia.
A trajetória de Gambiarra começou em 2015, inicialmente como malabarista nos semáforos da Região Metropolitana do Recife. No mesmo ano, passou a atuar como palhaço, realizando apresentações individuais e coletivas em praças públicas, feiras livres, escolas e comunidades urbanas e rurais.
O artista também integra o Coletivo Família Malanarquista, grupo recifense dedicado ao malabarismo, ao circo e à arte de rua. Ao longo de sua caminhada, desenvolveu produções próprias e percorreu diferentes cidades pernambucanas e outros estados, utilizando o chapéu como forma de contribuição direta do público para a valorização do trabalho artístico.
“A celebração de dez anos que olha para a memória seguindo adiante… do semáforo à praça, da praça ao palco, do palco à estrada, e da estrada a novos encontros e reencontros. Ao atravessar a Região Metropolitana, o Agreste e o Sertão, transforma-se uma história em cartografia afetiva. A estrada que antes foi percorrida em busca de espaços para apresentar-se, agora é transformada em caminho para reencontrar pessoas, compartilhar saberes, celebrar mestres, mestras e chegar às novas memórias”, declara.
Além das apresentações, “10 Anos Não São 10 Dias” inclui atividades formativas voltadas à troca de conhecimentos e à preservação da memória do circo pernambucano. Em setembro, os encontros aconteceram no Centro Comunitário Vivendo e Aprendendo (CCVA), em Camaragibe, com oficinas facilitadas por Luiza Fontes, Monick Pequeno e Renato Inácio.
A participação de artistas de diferentes gerações, incluindo referências como Índia Morena, natural de Jaboatão dos Guararapes, e os palhaços Pinóquio e Sequinho, contribui para a transmissão de experiências e para o fortalecimento das redes culturais.
“A proposta valoriza a memória do circo pernambucano com a participação de mestres, mestras e artistas que são de diferentes gerações. As rodas de diálogo surgem justamente da oralidade e da troca geracional como formas de transmissão e preservação dos saberes circenses. Em cada território, a apresentação se soma à formação e ao diálogo, criando possibilidades e aproximando públicos que nem sempre têm acesso contínuo à programação cultural”, afirma Gambiarra.
A realização é assinada pela GRAVE! Produtora e pelo Palhaço Gambiarra Produções Ilimitadas, produtoras pernambucanas. O projeto conta com incentivo da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc de Fomento à Cultura, por meio do Sistema Nacional de Cultura (SNC), do Ministério da Cultura e do Governo Federal.

https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.title: Burning rubbish chokes besieged Yemeni city of Taiz
https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.text:
Burning rubbish chokes besieged Yemeni city of Taiz
Taiz residents face health risks as waste accumulates amid sniper fire, forcing people to burn it in the streets.
Taiz, Yemen — Black smoke from burning rubbish envelops the Usaifira area north of the Yemeni city of Taiz, while foul odours fill the air in surrounding residential neighbourhoods.
Along a waterway known as the al-Saeed stream, bags of uncollected household waste pile up – a scene that has become part of daily life for residents. They find themselves trapped between mounds of rubbish and smoke, in a crisis that not only reflects a breakdown in public services but poses a direct threat to their health and environmental safety.
Since early October, the city has seen a buildup of waste, with sanitation trucks unable to reach the main landfill site in the western part of the city controlled by Iranian-backed Houthi forces, who have laid siege to the city for a month, affecting hundreds of thousands of people. Fighting has escalated since October 5, when forces of the internationally recognised government — backed by a Saudi-led military coalition — launched a major military offensive aimed at taking back all areas of the country under Houthi control.
Sanitation workers in Taiz say that snipers have been deployed in the vicinity of the landfill, and that staff have faced gunfire more than once while trying to reach the site to empty their trucks, preventing waste disposal operations.
The disruption comes as the city suffers from an acute shortage of fuel, which has further hampered waste collection. As a result, rubbish has accumulated on streets and in storm drains, prompting desperate residents to set the waste on fire.
The tide of rubbish extends into the stream from the middle of lower Tahrir Street down to the Usaifira area, in the middle of neighbourhoods where residents are exposed to toxic fumes every day.
Toxic health threats
Rather than a collection point, the al-Saeed stream has become a smoke-filled dumping ground, with fires igniting periodically and fumes drifting towards adjacent homes.
“This causes us suffocation and diseases, young and old. The children suffocate from the smoke,” Usaifira resident Abdo Hadi told Al Jazeera. “It is a foul smell, and on top of that they burn it.”
Hadi said the buildup and burning of waste are threatening the lives of his family and other residents, making already difficult living conditions even worse.
“We are besieged from every side, [with] neither gas nor petrol, and a black market,” he said.
Severe operational collapse
Taiz generates between 550 and 600 tonnes of waste daily, or about 16,500 to 18,000 tonnes per month. Mohammed Ibrahim, director of a cleaning initiative in Taiz, told Al Jazeera that waste collection has been severely affected since October 5.
Ibrahim said the cleaning initiative has also suffered from funding cuts, while supplies needed to carry out its work have been disrupted.
A sanitation worker described the grim reality while emptying a truck in Usaifira: “We are here with the rubbish in the Usaifira stream because of the war, and the people here are exposed to diseases from the rubbish, and we pile the waste in the stream, leave it to God.”
Escalating humanitarian crisis
The waste crisis is part of a wider breakdown of basic services in the city. On October 20, Laurent Bukera, the United Nations Humanitarian Coordinator for Yemen, expressed deep concern over the “rapidly deteriorating humanitarian and economic situation in Taiz”.
Bukera warned that road closures and insecurity were preventing vital supplies, including fuel, from entering the city and surrounding areas, leaving the health system “close to collapse”.
Emphasising the severe impact on hundreds of thousands of families, he warned that water production in the city has halved and alternatives are running out. Bukera called directly on the Houthis to urgently open safe passage for commercial goods, food, medicine, and humanitarian assistance in areas that they control.
The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has warned of an escalating humanitarian crisis in Taiz, saying conflict has cut off lifesaving assistance to 800,000 people, including 600,000 who depend on aid in the city.
El-Khidir Daloum, WFP representative and country director in Yemen, underlined the severity of the blockade.
“We are critically concerned about the escalating conflict, but even more so about the growing number of people we can no longer reach because of it,” Daloum said. “This is the kind of situation that can rapidly spiral into a humanitarian catastrophe if assistance cannot move safely and reach those who need it most.”
The blockade has also decimated local resources.
“Access roads have been cut off and that means that very little fuel, food or other supplies have reached the city since,” said Jens Laerke, spokesman for the UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
He explained that water production has fallen dramatically and the cost of trucked water has tripled.
“So, you can imagine what that does to these people who are trapped there,” Laerke added.
Health risks are multiplying rapidly in this polluted environment.
UNICEF has raised concerns about widespread hunger, saying it screened more than 168,000 children in Taiz this year, with more than 52,000 found to be acutely malnourished. Ricardo Pires, a spokesman for the UN children’s agency, warned of logistical hurdles.
“Even when stocks are available, access constraints and disruptions to supply routes can make it more difficult for partners to transport supplies and for families to safely reach treatment,” Pires said.

https://www.humanite.fr/-/-/a-toulouse-l.title: À Toulouse, les CRS empêchent le cortège d’avancer
https://www.humanite.fr/-/-/a-toulouse-l.text:
Après plus d’un mois de mouvement lycéen et des manifestations qui ont réuni des centaines de milliers de personnes dans les rues notamment les trois derniers samedis, l’heure est plus que jamais à la convergence des luttes ce jeudi 5 novembre. Augmentation des salaires, défense des services publics, justice fiscale, refus du budget d’austérité à 54 milliards soumis au parlement par Sébastien Lecornu…
Autant de mots d’ordre de l’intersyndicale pour cette journée de grève et de manifestations auxquels s’ajoutent les revendications de la jeunesse pour le droit d’étudier dans de bonnes conditions (remplacement des profs, réhabilitation des locaux, suppression de Parcoursup…).
1 512 appels à la grève et plus de 260 manifestations à travers l’Hexagone étaient recensés par la CGT ce jeudi matin. « Cela va être une belle mobilisation », observe Marylise Léon, secrétaire générale de la CFDT, avançant des remontées du même ordre que ce « qu’on avait sur les retraites ».
« Cette journée de grève a une double utilité : obtenir les hausses de salaire et contrer un budget qui fait payer aux travailleurs, aux précaires et aux retraités la facture des politiques en faveur des ultra-riches et des grandes entreprises », résume Thomas Vacheron, secrétaire confédéral CGT.
Le gouvernement, lui, continue de jouer la carte de la répression avec des manifestations entravées par les préfectures comme à Paris où le parcours, finalement au départ de République, n’a été arrêté qu’à la dernière minute. De son côté, le ministre de l’Intérieur Laurent Nuñez a annoncé mobiliser 70 000 policiers et gendarmes, promettant « une réponse d’une extrême fermeté » aux éventuels « débordements ». Face à la réponse autoritaire du gouvernement qui tente ainsi d’esquiver une réponse sur le fond des revendications, de nombreuses organisations ont dénoncé hier les attaques contre l’État de droit.

Germany: Lawyers demand judge recusal in Ulm 5 trial after Israeli arms expert barred
A German court has rejected applications by defence lawyers to hear expert witnesses in an ongoing trial of five activists alleged to have broken into an Israeli-owned arms factory.
Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo, who are from Germany, Spain, Ireland and the UK, were arrested on 8 September following an alleged break-in on the premises of Israeli arms firm Elbit Systems in the southwestern German city of Ulm.
Known as the “Ulm Five”, the group is accused of damaging the building's glass facade and smashing office equipment, including computers, screens and telephones.
They have been held for over a year in pretrial detention.
Defence lawyers told Middle East Eye that the court has either not responded to or rejected applications to hear from expert witnesses who could give testimony on the arms company’s role in Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

The legal team resorted to presenting two witnesses in person, as, under German law, a court is obliged to hear evidence from witnesses summoned by the defence if they filed an application to do so.
However, the court can reject the application if it deems the evidence to be inadmissible.
On 14 October the defence presented weapons expert Dr Shir Hever, who could speak about the connection between the technology developed at the Ulm site and Israel’s onslaught on Gaza.
After a day of deliberations the judge rejected the application, on the basis that the software developed at the laboratory had no connection with Israel’s offensive in Gaza.
The court then rejected another expert witness, international law expert Professor Isabel Feichtner, who was presented to give evidence on the genocide on 16 October.
Defence lawyer Benjamin Düsberg, who represents Tatlow-Devally, described the decision as “absurd”.
“The court has heard absolutely no evidence until now on this topic, so they just cannot know. And the expert was actually there to explain this connection,” he told MEE.
He added that, as a result, the defence team is submitting an application to demand Judge Kathrin Lauchstadt's recusal on the grounds of bias.
Speaking to reporters outside the court on Friday, Dusberg rejected the proceedings as “a pure show trial”.
The activists are alleged to have damaged the Tactical Data Links (TDL) laboratory housed at Elbit’s Ulm site.
Also speaking at the press conference, Hever explained that TDL is a network which allows Israeli soldiers to communicate and to share locations of targets. That information is then sent to a cloud called the Nimbus Project – produced by Amazon and Google – and then analysed by AI in order to generate mass targets.
'The witnesses either seem to all suffer from the identical amnesia or refuse to testify by invoking the limitations on their authorisation to testify'
– Nina Oner, defence lawyer
“So the way that this genocide is happening in Gaza is indeed unprecedented because it can produce targets on an industrial scale,” Hever explained.
“This is why the action of the five was justified,” Düsberg said, emphasising that the laboratory had “been extremely important for the conduct of this war”.
He stressed the fact that the defendants had targeted “precisely the laboratory where the technology is developed, must be taken into consideration”.
Düsberg added: “The court said, 'We assume there is no connection', but without knowing anything, and they cannot, because none of their witnesses could say anything about the technical questions of the production in Ulm.”
Stuttgart's regional court told MEE in response to a request for comment that it does not comment on “the conduct of the proceedings by the presiding judge, or the behaviour of those involved in the trial”.
The court confirmed that the two witnesses presented by the defence had been rejected, and that “no decisions have yet been made” on the remaining evidence applications submitted by the team.
Collective amnesia
Defence lawyers and defendants’ family members told MEE that successive police witnesses had told the court they were instructed by the prosecution not to investigate Elbit Systems’ activities in relation to Israel’s genocide in Gaza.
According to Mimi Tatlow-Golden, Tatlow-Devally’s mother, one police officer, Mr Herold, who was tasked with investigating Elbit’s finances, told the court that he had noted that 38 percent of Elbit’s profits went abroad.
“He was asked if he looked to see where that was going and he said no. So he said, 'Oh, anyway, I'm not a technical expert on weapons, and I don't know anything about this. It's not my area,'” Tatlow-Golden told MEE.
Under German law, the public prosecutor is obligated to investigate both incriminating and exculpatory circumstances.
Defence lawyers said that police witnesses called by the prosecution were unable to answer questions in cross-examination, citing memory loss or confidentiality.
“Whenever we get to the really interesting questions, the witnesses either seem to all suffer from the identical amnesia or refuse to testify by invoking the limitations on their authorisation to testify,” lawyer Nina Oner, who represents Hailu, told MEE.
On 25 August the court heard evidence from an investigating officer from the Stuttgart State Criminal Police Office (LKA), Ms Jager. She was tasked with processing the defendants at the Ulm-Mitte police station on 8 September, where they were being held following their arrest.
Tatlow-Golden said that Jager told the court that she could not recall any details relating to her interactions with the defendants.
“I’ve never seen anything like it. She couldn’t remember anything,” Tatlow-Golden told MEE. “She didn’t remember what the conditions were like. She didn't remember whether they asked for lawyers, or anything like that. She didn’t remember what time anything happened. She just kept not remembering.
'She didn't remember whether they asked for lawyers… She didn’t remember what time anything happened. She just kept not remembering'
– Defendant's mother, on police officer
“And I can only imagine that the reason that she claims not to remember anything is because she was the one who was in charge at the police station where they were held when they were supposed to have been read their rights,” Tatlow-Golden said, adding that this did not happen for 12 hours and that the five were denied access to their lawyers and contact with family.
LKA told MEE in response to a request for comment that it does not comment on ongoing investigations.
Tatlow-Golden said that Jager could also not recall multiple attempts by the defendants’ lawyers to speak with their clients. Tatlow-Devally identified Jäger as the officer that he had kept asking to allow him a call to his lawyer and his father.
"Daniel's evidence was that Ms Jäger would just say 'later'," Tatlow-Golden said.
Oner said that the defence team had repeatedly asked police witnesses about the involvement of the interior ministry or German intelligence services in the investigation.
“Usually we get the answer that basically this is confidential information, and they cannot answer our questions,” Onèr told MEE.
“We have been told by the witnesses that there have been meetings with the prosecutor, and that other people were involved, but we were not told who these other people were, and the only logical reason why that would be is because that is German intelligence services,” she added.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Alertas de bomba em mais de 10 voos provocam pousos de emergência na Europa
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Uma onda de ameaças de bomba atingiu ao menos 12 voos no espaço aéreo europeu nesta quinta-feira (5), forçando desvios de rota e procedimentos de emergência em diversos países do continente. Os incidentes somam-se a outros sete alertas registrados na última terça-feira (3), ocasião em que a operação do aeroporto de Varsóvia, na Polônia, precisou ser interrompida temporariamente.
Em Bruxelas, na Bélgica, autoridades europeias declararam ser “muito cedo” para confirmar se os episódios registrados ao longo da semana possuem ligação entre si. Até o momento, nenhum artefato explosivo foi encontrado após a inspeção das aeronaves pelas equipes de segurança.
Entre as rotas afetadas nesta quinta, um Airbus A320 da companhia irlandesa Aer Lingus, que viajava de Dublin, na Irlanda, para Roma, na Itália, com 151 passageiros e seis tripulantes a bordo, declarou emergência sobre o norte da França. A aeronave foi escoltada por caças militares Rafale até a base aérea de Évreux, na Normandia, onde os ocupantes desembarcaram em segurança.
Outros incidentes envolveram voos da Finnair partindo de Helsinque, na Finlândia, com destino a Viena, na Áustria, e Roma; uma rota da companhia LOT entre Varsóvia e Bruxelas; uma viagem da Wizz Air de Milão a Bucareste; e quatro trajetos rumo a Praga, na República Tcheca.
Os episódios ocorrem em um cenário de elevada tensão geopolítica no continente europeu, marcado por denúncias de ações de guerra híbrida e incursões não autorizadas de drones no espaço aéreo da região. Nenhuma organização assumiu a autoria dos alertas de segurança.
